title: Cosmos and Cocoa
location: Robert Ferguson Observatory, 2605 Adobe Canyon Road, Kenwood, CA
description:
Begin your evening with a guided hike along our Planet Walk Trail, a flat and scenic journey to Saturn and back, approximately 1.2 miles in total, beneath the darkening sky as knowledgeable docents offer insightful facts at each planetary stop. Did you know: each step in our planet walk is equivalent to 2.3 million miles through our solar system! 
After the walk, return to the Robert Ferguson Observatory to warm up with a cup of hot cocoa and an in-depth stargazing session led by one of our experienced astronomers. The night sky tour blends science and storytelling, helping you appreciate the night sky in a whole new way. 
Once the Star guide portion concludes, guests are welcome to refill their cocoa and continue observing through our telescopes for the remainder of the night. 
This program is designed for families and guests of all ages who can comfortably enjoy a light hike and remain respectful and attentive while volunteers offer information. Please wear appropriate footwear and bring a white-light flashlight for this event only.

title: Thomas Cassell and Nick Fallon at Out West Garage
location: Out West Garage, 321 Second Street, Petaluma, 94952, United States
description:
Originally from the sacred bluegrass mountains of southwestern Virginia, Thomas Cassell stands among the top tier of modern bluegrass musicians. A member of the Wood Box Heroes, he’s made numerous Grand Ole Opry appearances, in addition to building an accomplished history as a sideman with artists such as Trey Hensley, Nefesh Mountain, Billy Strings, Bryan Sutton, and more. 
Cassell’s most recent album release, Guitar Collection (2026), highlights an impressive roster of collaborators with each of its tracks featuring a different guest artist, including Tim Stafford, Trey Hensley, Nick Fallon, and more. 
Nick Fallon is a progressive bluegrass guitarist, singer, and songwriter from Floyd, Virginia, now making his mark in Nashville’s vibrant acoustic scene, having toured extensively across the U.S. and internationally as a member of the acclaimed Tray Wellington Band and with the genre- blurring comedy-grass outfit, The Cleverlys. 
Together, Thomas Cassell & Nick Fallon offer audiences a listening experience that feels at once deeply rooted and refreshingly modern – equal parts intimate and virtuosic – showcasing just how expansive contemporary bluegrass can be. 
Call 707-477-6309 for reservations

description: For the Diné, weaving is considered a ceremony. This exhibit features rugs from the SRJC Multicultural Museum's collections, featuring award winning woven rugs such as a fine "Burntwater" style rug by the great Nellie Roan and many other examples of Navajo rugs from the 1920s through the 1970s.More information available on the SRJC Multicultural Museum website. description: Viansa Winery feels made for live music, perched atop the Summit of Sonoma with sweeping vineyard views and Tuscan-inspired charm. title: Tom Chown: 46 Years Behind the Lens
location: Robert F. Agrella Art Gallery - Santa Rosa Campus
description: Santa Rosa Junior College will celebrate the 46-year career of longtime staff photographer Tom Chown with a photography exhibition featuring images from his decades at the college, from the days of film and darkrooms to the digital era.  Chown began his career at SRJC at age 24, working in the campus photography lab. Over the next 46 years, he became a familiar presence throughout the college community, documenting the people, programs and milestones that shaped generations of students and employees.  The exhibition will trace Chown's evolution as a photographer, from working with film and developing photographs in the darkroom to embracing digital photography. It also offers a visual history of SRJC, preserving moments from nearly five decades of college life.  The exhibition is free and open to the public.Location: Robert F. Agrella Art Gallery, Doyle Library 1st floor - Santa Rosa CampusFor more information, visit SRJC's Robert F. Agrella Art Gallery website. In this 4 session intensive, students will create work for a soda firing while learning the history and chemistry of atmospheric Soda. Each session there will be demos and assignments that will lend to intentional and experimental decisions on the objects we make for the firing. We will make tests in clay material, slips, glazes, experiment in wadding, and placements in the kiln. During class there will be lectures on the chemistry of clay and of soda firing as well as its history, application, and experiments within the field. This class is about learning how to explore what soda can do.During the 4 weeks each student will create one cubic foot of work to be bisqued and then fired in the soda kiln. The firing will be two full days of activity, with students applying the lessons learned in class to the wadding and loading of the kiln and lighting the kiln. Students will learn how to plan a gas kiln schedule, use a kiln log, assess a kilns needs, and successfully fire off a kiln. Students will learn how to spray soda and how to maintain the kiln and her accessories in order to support Julia’s \(our beloved soda kiln\) longevity. This deep dive into soda will spark ideas and expand folx knowledge on kilns, firing, and making in clay.

title: Meditation in the Orchard with Joy Jacobsen at Gold Ridge Organic Farm
location: Gold Ridge Organic Farms
description:
Start your Sunday with a peaceful introduction to meditation in the tranquil setting of our olive orchard. Led by registered yoga teacher, Joy Jacobsen, this session offers an opportunity to simply be with yourself, surrounded by nature, listening to the gentle vibrations of the world in a safe, peaceful, and restorative space.

We'll begin with a peaceful stroll to the orchard from our Farm Shop. Feel free to bring your own mat, though we'll also provide one if needed. Then we'll move into gentle standing stretches and mindful breathing—essential practices that prepare the body to become limber, relaxed, and comfortable for stillness. As you settle into a 20-minute meditation, Joy will hold space for your practice, opening and closing the session with the soothing sound of a singing bowl.

We'll conclude the experience back at the farm shop with fresh apple cider and sliced heirloom apples.

Joy brings firsthand experience from training in Hatha and Vinyasa yoga in Goa, India, and from completing a three-week silent meditation retreat in Thailand. Her welcoming, supportive approach creates an ideal environment for both experienced practitioners and those new to meditation. You'll also find her warmth at Gold Ridge Organic Farms, where she manages the Farm Shop and is a familiar, friendly face to our community.
source: North Bay Bohemian, Press Democrat, Sebastopol Calendar

title: Meditative Birding California Biodiversity Day 2026
location: Sugarloaf Ridge State Park
description:
We will start off by sitting quietly for 10 minutes with Merlin app recording in 3 different locations, followed by about 10 minutes of discussion of the birds we heard, using Cornell to confirm their calls and songs before moving onto the next sitting spot. We will also saunter (while looking for birds) between the locations for a total distance of ~1.3 mile & ~250’ ascent. Birding by ear lends itself to meditation because it works best when you sit silently and listening closely (i.e., if Merlin *hears* something you did not, it reminds you that your mind has wandered).

Meet at the White Barn parking lot. Tickets are $10 for general audiences, $5 for students, youth (12-17 year olds; must be accompanied by a parent or legal guardian), Sugarlof members, Sugarloaf or RFO volunteers, and free for children under 12. **Tickets day-of on site are $15 and might not be available**. 

Ensure you install the Merlin app on your device along with the bird pack for US: West Coast before you arrive for the hike, as there is no cell service is non-existent in the areas we'll be meandering. Wear layers (it's likely to be cold in the early morning) and sturdy shoes. Bring binoculars, at least a quart of water, sun protection, a bird-identification guide (if you have one), and if desired, a snack. If you are willing to carry a portable chair for about 1.3 miles, you are welcome to bring it, but there will be benches at all of our stops. Parking fees apply.
source: North Bay Bohemian, Press Democrat, Visit Santa Rosa

title: Henry Frank: J-80928: A Human Experience Exhibition
location: San Geronimo Valley Community Center
description:
The San Geronimo Valley Community Center is proud to present featured September artist **Henry Frank** in the Del Mue Galleries this September. There will be a reception for the artist as part of the International Day of Peace Festival Finale on **September 20 from 2 – 6 pm**.

**J-80928: A Human Experience Exhibition** explores Henry Frank’s transformative journey through nearly three decades of incarceration in the California Department of Corrections. Through deeply personal artwork, the exhibition reflects on trauma, friendship, identity, hope, and personal growth while inviting viewers to recognize the humanity and capacity for change in people who are incarcerated.

**ARTISTS STATEMENT** **J-80928: A Human Experience Exhibition** explores my personal journey serving a 29-year-to-life sentence in the California Department of Corrections as an Indigenous person, an artist, and a human being. I was incarcerated from February 15, 1994, to April 19, 2013, and during much of that time, I lived hour to hour. For the first 14 years, my mantras were: expect the worst and hope for the best, trust no one except myself, and fear is a state of mind. While many experiences were deeply traumatic, there were also moments of humanity, compassion, joy, and empathy that transformed how I saw myself and the world around me.

The last six years of my incarceration became the most transformative period of my life. I began to believe that I would not die in prison. I found hope, discovered the importance of serving others, began to see myself as a serious artist, and gained a deeper understanding of my place in the world. My mantras evolved into: expect the best and be prepared for anything less, trust everyone until they give me a reason not to, and happiness is a choice. During this time, I learned to love and respect myself, to be accountable, to live in the present, to be a true friend, and to serve others with intention and compassion.

This exhibition is an oeuvre dedicated to the experiences, emotional trauma, friendships, and reclamation of identity that shaped me throughout my incarceration. Through this body of work, I hope people can connect with parts of my journey and recognize that I am not so different from them. More importantly, I want to humanize those who are currently incarcerated and raise awareness that people are capable of change. They can become contributing members of their communities. They have families, hobbies, hopes, dreams, and the capacity for growth and transformation.

I have been working toward completing this body of work and plan to have the exhibition finished completely by the end of this year.

This exhibition is partially funded by an Artist Fellowship Grant from the Art for Justice Fund. I am grateful for their support and patience for this exhibition to evolve into its fullest potential.

Human Being

Henry Edward Frank

Yurok and Kashaya Pomo

title: Art Exhibit: Painting in Fauve
location: Upstairs Art Gallery
description:
Date: FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE  7/15/26

AUGUST EXHIBIT: PAINTING IN FAUVE

EXHIBIT DATES:  July 27 – August 30, 2026

RECEPTION: SATURDAY, August 1, 2026, 3-6 pm: Join us to meet Willow LaLand and Gen Zorich;  Learn about their art and celebrate the show.  Be sure to take part in the Gallery’s free monthlong drawing for a beautiful work by a Gallery artist.  Refreshments will be served.

Sonoma wine country artist, Willow LaLand presents Painting in Fauve, a collection of oil and acrylic paintings focusing on our region’s vibrant beauty through the artist’s Fauvist lens.  Known for her hyper-realistic landscapes, these works take an imaginative turn to the fantastical, tapping into the wild Fauve vivid color palette.   Highlighting the show, “Mt. Tamalpais” comes alive, swathed in rich colors cascading over its undulating slopes, while rich foreground purple/blues heighten the mountain’s grandeur.  “Fitch Mountain” similarly seems to sing with color as it overlooks a lush vineyard.  LaLand’s color lens takes us from palette to palate as she captures the luxuriant purple/reds of a fine red wine in “Sommelier’s Dream.”  Reflecting on her creative process, LaLand notes “I love the artistic freedom to play, create depth in color, and give a tangible realistic impression within a completely fantastical expression.”

A third-generation artist, LaLand started her studies as a young girl and had a studio space at 10 years old.  She is inspired by early American realists and uses traditional techniques to achieve dramatic realism.  LaLand finds the Fauve color palette elicits a joyful response to her themes of nature and wine.  Many of her collectors love both her styles and have a hard time, though they vastly differ, choosing between the two.  LaLand exhibits widely, including internationally, and participated in the Art Trails Program.  She was featured in American Art Collector magazine in 2013 and on KRCB in 2015.

Meet the artist: LaLand will host the Gallery on August 2, 2:30 – 6pm and August 16 & 29, 11am to 6 pm.

The Stairway Smallworks Showcase features Gen Zorich’s Summertime, highlighting the beauty of wine country and the warmth of long, lazy summer days.  From Zorich’s background as a geologist and environmental scientist, she imbues her paintings with a deep understanding of the natural world. Focusing on flora, pink waterlilies floating on pastel pads in “Summer Color” engender a sense of sun-filled easy days.  These works would bring a feeling of summer contentment any time of year.  An award-winning artist, Zorich has exhibited widely and has been a longtime participant in the Sonoma County Art Trails Program.

Meet the artist: Zorich will host the Gallery on August 2, 11am – 2:30pm, August 4, 11am to 6 pm and August 21 & 23, 2:30 – 6pm.

Also join us for ART NITE HEALDSBURG, Thursday, August 6, 5 – 7 pm.  ART NITE Healdsburg, held the 1st Thursday of Every Month, is a community event celebrating art and creativity with over 20 galleries participating. This month’s special theme: Music and Mocktails.  ArtNiteHealdsburg.com.

For further information: Contact: Beverly Bird, Press Contact, at bvdrio@sonic.net or 707-799-1490.

title: ART EXHIBIT:  THE DAYS OF VINES AND ROSES
location: Upstairs Art Gallery
description:
EPTEMBER ART EXHIBIT:  THE DAYS OF VINES AND ROSES

Date: FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE  8/12/26

DATES: August 31 – September 27, 2026

RECEPTION:  SATURDAY, September 5 – 3 -6 pm Join Donna Schaffer and Tosya Shore to celebrate the show and learn about their artistic inspirations.  Refreshments will be served.  

Featured Artist Donna Schaffer Celebrates Wine Country Beauty in “The Days of Vines and Roses”

Sonoma County artist Donna Schaffer unveils her latest collection of oil paintings, “The Days of Vines and Roses,” celebrating some of her favorite views of roses blooming among the vineyards, hills, and woodlands of Sonoma County. At the heart of the collection is Vines and Trellis of Roses, where glorious pink roses spill across an entrance trellis, set against the orderly rows of a vineyard. In Mini Red Roses Along Vineyard, delicate red roses punctuate the landscape, creating a lively interplay between vineyard rows, stands of trees, and the hills beyond. “Living here in Sonoma County for three decades, I never tire of its glorious natural beauty. It is an enduring inspiration and truly a painter’s dream,” says Schaffer.

Art has been a focus throughout Schaffer’s life. She has been painting full time in Dry Creek since the mid-1990s and is particularly known for her paintings of Sonoma County’s wine country. Her work are popular with both locals and visitors who want to bring a bit of Sonoma’s beauty and magic into their own homes. Schaffer has been a member of the Upstairs Art Gallery for more than 25 years and has exhibited regionally, including eight years as an Art Trails artist.

Meet the artist:  Schaffer will be hosting the Gallery on September 3 and 27 from 11-6 pm.  

Stairway Showcase: Tosya Shore — “It’s Black and White with a Splash of Color”

The Stairway Showcase presents artist Tosya Shore’s “It’s Black and White with a Splash of Color,” a collection of watercolors that begins with the fundamentals of composition: reducing an image to its two most essential elements—black and white. Working with ink, a stick, and a scraper, Shore roughens the edges of her subjects and strips away unnecessary detail, allowing light itself—not form or precision—to take center stage. Her paintings invite the viewer to experience the essence of a scene through contrast, gesture, and the expressive qualities of the medium.

In addition to her watercolor works, Shore presents paintings inspired by a recent trip to Carmel, where she picked up oil paint for the first time and explored painting the ocean using nothing but a palette knife. The resulting works introduce a vibrant splash of color and texture into a practice grounded in restraint—new pigment, new surface, yet the same enduring fascination with light over likeness.

title: Nothing To See Here - Jason Perry
location: Mare Island Art Studios
description:
"Nothing To See Here" is a critical, yet playful examination of the UFO phenomenon that is hinged on the dynamic between serious scientific inquiry and fringe science.

With a mixed media approach that combines drawing, collage, and painting, Jason Perry seeks to entice the viewer into the work through familiar visual iconography, bold colors, expressive marks, and textures. Once there, the viewer is offered a deeper layer of meaning to consider. Perry calls into question the blurred narratives, misinformation, and potential truths surrounding the UFO topic.

At its core, "Nothing To See Here" invites us to look a little closer at our beliefs, our relationship to the strange, the unexplained, and our enduring fascination with what might be out there.

description: Callie Watts is a singer/songwriter from Northern California who was raised on classical music, The Beatles and The Beach Boys before discovering Joni Mitchell, Elton John, Stevie Wonder, Paul Simon, Billy Joel, Carole King, and all the great writers of the ’60s and 70’s who have influenced her sound and writing style. After graduating high school, Callie began playing and performing solo, as well as in local and bay area bands of different genres. She’s played blues with Eric Lindell and the Reds, funky soul with Phatty, and jazz/swing with Savoy Swingers along with many other various projects. Callie has taken turns throughout her career as a keyboardist, guitarist, writer, and lead/backing vocalist, and she’s currently a member of the dynamic Sonoma County funk rock band Burrows and Dilbeck, having joined in 2010 as part of the former band Frobeck. Over time, she’s had the honor of opening for acts such as Bootsy Collins, Elvin Bishop, Huey Lewis and The News, War, Ozomatli, Bill Champlin, Booker T, and the B52s. Callie continues to perform frequently as an acoustic solo artist, focusing on developing a core audience and a buzz for her original material. You can help preserve our heritage by joining us for a free, fun community event

title: FIESTA DE INDEPENDENCIA
location: Luther Burbank Center for the Arts
description:
Celebrate Hispanic Heritage Month with a taste of Latin America in Sonoma County! Enjoy authentic food, music, games, and activities for the entire family. Organized by the Center’s Latino Advisory Council, this free, family-friendly, campus-wide festival honors Latin American countries that recognize their independence during this month.

LBC also will present its annual Community Leadership Awards in partnership with Los Cien Sonoma County to an individual and an organization that have demonstrated an outstanding commitment to the Latino Community through volunteerism, education, mentorship, or other personal or professional efforts.

Fiesta de Independencia began at the Center in 2010 to commemorate Mexican Independence Day \(September 16\) and has since evolved to celebrate the rich history of the diverse Latino cultures and people who are an integral part of the North Bay community. Drawing more than 5,000 community members each year, the event has become a Sonoma County tradition. The Fiesta is a community-wide celebration of cultures, people, and traditions that also increases awareness about Hispanic history and tradition, service organizations that support our community, and the many Latinx businesses in Sonoma County.

¡Celebre el mes de la herencia hispana con una muestra de América Latina en el condado de Sonoma! Disfrute de auténtica comida, música, juegos y actividades para toda la familia.  Organizado por el Consejo Asesor Latino del Centro, este festival gratuito, familiar y que se llevará a cabo en todo el campus honra a los países latinoamericanos que reconocen su independencia durante este mes.

LBC también presentará sus Premios Anuales  de Liderazgo Comunitario en conjunto con Los Cien del Condado de Sonoma a un individuo y a una organización que hayan demostrado un compromiso sobresaliente con la comunidad latina a través del voluntariado, la educación, la tutoría u otros esfuerzos personales o profesionales.

La Fiesta de Independencia comenzó en el Centro en 2010 para conmemorar el Día de la Independencia de México \(16 de septiembre\) y desde entonces ha evolucionado para celebrar la rica historia de las diversas culturas y latinoamericanos que son parte integral de la comunidad del Norte de la Bahía. Atrayendo a más de 5,000 miembros de la comunidad cada año, el evento se ha convertido en una tradición del Condado de Sonoma. La Fiesta es una celebración comunitaria de culturas, personas y tradiciones que también aumenta la conciencia sobre la historia y la tradición hispanas, las organizaciones de servicio que apoyan a nuestra comunidad y las muchas empresas latinas en el condado de Sonoma.

title: Equivocation
location: Spreckels Center for the Performing Arts
description: England, 1605: A terrorist plot is brewing to assassinate King James 1 and blow Parliament to kingdom come! Or so the King claims. To spread his propaganda, King James 1 hires the world’s most famous playwright, William Shagspeare \(after a contemporary spelling of the Bard’s name\). As Shag investigates the King’s bizarre tale, he begins to question it, leading him and his actors to a dilemma: lie and pocket the cash, tell the truth and literally risk their necks, or perhaps equivocate–lie and tell the truth at the same time. This high-stakes thriller drops into many of the Bard’s most famous works in an alternate history that resonates today. This is a witty and poignant ensemble piece in which six actors play well over a dozen roles, some of which include snippets of Shakespeare's other plays-in-progress \(one of which becomes the famous Macbeth.\)

title: South Pacific
location: 6th Street Playhouse
description:
**An unforgettable romance set against the sweeping tides of World War II.**

Against the backdrop of the Pacific War of WWII, ***South Pacific*** blends high-stakes wartime romance with a poignant exploration of social prejudice. When spirited Navy nurse, Nellie Forbush, falls in love with a sophisticated French planter, and a young Marine lieutenant finds himself captivated by an ethereal island girl, their relationships are tested by the prejudices and pressures of a world at war. What unfolds is a deeply moving story about love, courage, and the transformative power of understanding. Featuring a soaring score by **Richard Rodgers** and **Oscar Hammerstein II**, including classics like “Some Enchanted Evening” and “There Is Nothin’ Like a Dame,” *South Pacific* remains one of the most beloved musicals of all time.

Winner of the 1950 Pulitzer Prize for Drama, the original Broadway production won ten Tony Awards, including Best Musical, Best Score and Best Libretto. It is the only musical production ever to have won all four Tony Awards for acting.

SOUTH PACIFIC is presented by arrangement with Concord Theatricals on behalf of The Rodgers & Hammerstein Organization. concordtheatricals.com

Performances run Thur, Friday, Saturday evenings at 7:30pm and Saturday and Sunday matinees at 2:00pm.

title: Myth & Archetype as seen through Poetry & Astrology
location: Occidental Center for the Arts, 3850 Doris Murphy Court, Occidental, CA 95465
description:
We invite all to a fascinating afternoon with Diana and Brian who will explore through the respective lenses of astrology and poetry, valuable insights offered by both myth and archetype, for better clarity and resilience in today’s tumultuous world.
This event features Author and Astrologer Diana Badger discussing her book "
Dance of the Archetypes: How Astrology Informs our Lives and Connects Us to the Earth",
and Author/Poet/Storyteller Brian R. Martens with his book,
"Merlin’s Wing", Mythic Poems.
This event is free, all donations gratefully invited. Selected readings from each presenter, a storytelling with Brian, then Q&A, book sales & signing
.
Refreshments for sale. OCA’s facilities are accessible to people with disabilities.
Dance of the Archetypes
by Diana Badger
Whether you’re new to astrology or already immersed in its symbolism,
Dance of the Archetypes
illuminates the zodiac in a refreshingly accessible way. With grounded wisdom, Diana connects planetary cycles to the Earth we depend on, our emotional lives, and our healing. This is a beautifully integrative guide for readers seeking relevance, connection, and purpose in rapidly changing times, brought to life by the author’s own striking photographs.
For the past 20 years, Diana Badger has woven together parallel careers as a counseling astrologer and a writer/editor, while pursuing an ongoing commitment to inner work and spiritual practice. Rooted in a reverence for the natural world and informed by multiple wisdom traditions, Diana’s work reflects a lifelong inquiry into the relationship between psyche, cosmos, and Earth. She currently devotes her time to her
Earth Sky Journal
podcast/writing, her astrology practice, tending of her garden, and adventures in local community.
Merlin’s Wing
by Brian Martens
This collection of poems is concerned with the “Human Condition” : Awareness, Transformation, and Deep Intuition. His poetry resonates with yearning, humor and intelligence in which he expresses his love and admiration for the first people, the ancestors, animal, human and plant. He asks these voices to speak through him in symbols, rhythms and revelations to reveal the deep beauty, tragedy, and unknowable mystery that surrounds him.
Brian R. Martens is an abstract Artist, Poet, Author, Creativity Facilitator, International Speaker, Myth Maker, CA Poets in the Schools Instructor, Podcaster, and Storyteller. Brian weaves poetry, myth, and reflection into all his storytelling. His first book,
Three Raven Gate
, is a collection of haiku, the form he learned from his work with Angeles Arrien Ph.D., a cross-cultural anthropologist, over the course of seven years. Brian seeks to inspire and motivate people, with articles, podcasts, creativity workshops, and poetry to recognize their own deep creative spirit and to express that to the world.

title: Tommy Castro
location: Rancho Nicasio
description:
Multiple award-winning, California-based blues and rock sensation Tommy Castro is the guitar slinging, soul-singing leader of the telepathically tight and wildly raucous Tommy Castro & The Painkillers \(bassist Randy McDonald, keyboardist Dave Fleschner and drummer Stewart Burr\). He’s released 17 previous albums over the course of his four-decade career. Each release features its own individual sound and style, ranging from horn-fueled R&B to piping hot blues and soul to fiery, stripped-down rock ‘n’ roll. With his new album, Closer To The Bone, Castro has returned to his roots, delivering what he calls “a real blues record, the way they would have made them back in the day.” Closer To The Bone is the most unvarnished, straight-ahead blues release of Castro’s career, one that bristles with every ounce of his dynamic energy and raw emotion.  

On Closer To The Bone \(Castro’s 8th Alligator release\), Castro mixes new Castro originals \(Ain’t Worth The Heartache, Can’t Catch A Break, Crazy Woman Blues\) with songs originally performed by many of Castro’s friends and heroes. Artists and their songs include Johnny Nitro \(One More Night, on which Castro plays his treasured 1966 black Fender Stratocaster, a guitar once owned by Nitro himself\), Magic Slim \(Hole In The Wall\), Ron Thompson \(Freight Train\), Mike Duke \(Keep Your Dog Inside\) and Chris Cain \(Woke Up And Smelled The Coffee\). Castro additionally chose obscure songs by Wynonie Harris \(Bloodshot Eyes\), Eddie Taylor \(Stroll Out West\), Jimmy Nolen \(The Way You Do\) and Johnny “Guitar” Watson \(She Moves Me\). According to Castro, “These are not the obvious artists people generally cover, and that was most definitely on purpose.”  

Closer To The Bone was produced by master guitarist and studio wizard Christoffer “Kid” Andersen \(producer of over 100 albums\), at his now-famous Greaseland Studio in San Jose, California. Closer To The Bone finds Castro at the top of his game, bringing his seemingly limitless energy and boundless talent to the studio. Guests on the album include labelmates Andersen, Rick Estrin, Chris Cain and Billy Branch, along with saxophone player/vocalist Deanna Bogart, keyboard wizard Jim Pugh and, on three songs, the voices of The Sons Of The Soul Revivers. 

Born in San Jose, California in 1955, Tommy Castro first picked up a guitar at age 10. He fell under the spell of six-string stars like Elvin Bishop, Taj Mahal and Mike Bloomfield. Almost every major rock and soul act, from Ike and Tina Turner to Janis Joplin to Tower Of Power, toured through the area, and Castro was at every show. He saw John Lee Hooker, Albert King, and Buddy Guy and Junior Wells at a local club, JJ’s Blues Bar. Castro often jammed at JJ’s, dreaming of busting out and making a name for himself. He created his own personal sound and style by mixing the blues, R&B and funk music he loved into his own, instantly recognizable brand of uplifting, soul-healing music. 

As his reputation spread, Tommy played in several Bay Area bands, quickly making a name for himself as a hotter-than-hot live artist bursting at the seams with talent. In 1985, he became lead singer and guitarist for the regionally popular blues band NiteCry before joined popular Warner Brothers’ artists The Dynatones, gigging all over the country. He formed the first Tommy Castro Band in 1992 and has not stopped touring since. In 1995, soon after releasing their first album on Blind Pig Records, The Tommy Castro Band were selected as the house band for three seasons on NBC Television’s Comedy Showcase \(airing right after Saturday Night Live\). The show brought Tommy in front of millions of viewers every week and cemented his reputation as a not-to-be-missed live performer.   

After a series of successful releases on the Blind Pig, Telarc and 33rd Street labels, Tommy Castro joined Alligator Records in 2009. His label debut, Hard Believer, launched to massive popular and critical acclaim. 2011 saw the release of the raucous Tommy Castro Presents The Legendary Rhythm & Blues Revue—Live!. In 2014, Castro & The Painkillers released The Devil You Know, followed by Method To My Madness in 2015, Stompin’ Ground in 2017, and the irresistible Killin’ It—Live in 2019. With 2021’s A Bluesman Came To Town, Castro told the story of a young musician’s journey through the blues world. AllMusic said the album was “a towering achievement.”  

Castro received his fourth prestigious and coveted Blues Music Award for B.B. King Entertainer Of The Year in 2023. He’s taken home a total of 10 Blues Music Awards and is among the genre’s most decorated artists. Castro’s relentless road-dog approach—gig after gig, 150 nights a year—continues to earn him loyal, lifelong fans everywhere he plays. The Washington Post says Castro is “phenomenal and funky” with “soulful vocals and inspired blues guitar.” Famed guitarist Joe Bonamassa says, “Tommy has always been top of the heap among blues guitar players. He always puts on a great show.”

 Tommy Castro & The Painkillers’ deceptively simple approach on Closer To The Bone delivers one thrilling performance after another. Says Castro, “Here, I’m not the contemporary guy, not the rock guy, not the soul guy. This is the deeper blues side of me. I know, with these songs, I am at my most authentic.”

description:
The Inn at Occidental is proud to welcome back our Sunset Concert Series for 2026. Join us on select Sunday evenings as live music fills the courtyard and the sun sets over West Sonoma County. ABOUT Carlos Reyes 
“Santana meets the Gipsy Kings” 
Born in Paraguay and performing publicly since the age of five, Carlos Reyes has spent a lifetime redefining what the Paraguayan harp and violin can do. A child prodigy who began studying violin at three, he soon took up the traditional 36-string Paraguayan harp, turning an early challenge from his father into a lifelong musical path. 
By his teens, Carlos had already debuted with the Oakland Symphony and Oakland Youth Symphony and was working in professional recording studios. He went on to build an international career as a recording artist, producer, and multi-instrumentalist. 
His debut album The Beauty of It All spent more than 15 weeks in Billboard’s Top Ten Contemporary Jazz charts, launching a career that has taken him across Europe, Asia, and the Americas. Along the way he has performed and recorded with artists including Steve Miller, Willie Nelson, Chuck Mangione, and The Doobie Brothers. 
Blending Latin, jazz, rock, and classical influences, Carlos brings a bold and innovative voice to the harp, expanding the instrument’s possibilities both acoustically and electronically. Whether performing solo or with a full ensemble, his performances combine virtuosity, passion, and a deeply expressive musical spirit.

Join us for two special evenings with the community storytellers featured in Belongings: What We Bring, What We Leave Behind. Through family heirlooms, treasured keepsakes, photographs, letters, and everyday belongings, participants will share the deeply personal stories that bring the exhibition to life. 

Hear firsthand reflections on migration, identity, resilience, family, and the meaning of home. These intimate conversations offer a rare opportunity to connect directly with the individuals whose voices and objects are featured throughout the exhibition, creating space for dialogue, empathy, and shared understanding. 

Following the storytelling program, continue the conversation while exploring the exhibition and enjoying light refreshments. 

Stories We Carry is presented as part of Belongings: What We Bring, What We Leave Behind, on view September 4–October 4, 2026, at the Petaluma Historical Library & Museum. The exhibition explores migration, memory, and belonging through the meaningful objects and personal stories that connect us across generations and cultures. 

Belongings: What We Bring, What We Leave Behind is made possible through the generous support of California Humanities through its Connecting California grant program. We are also deeply grateful to our community partners and sponsors, including the North Bay Asian American Pacific Islander Coalition, Sonoma County Japanese American Citizens League, Petaluma Arts Center, Life on Art, Zimbabwe Cultural Exchange Project of California, El Día de los Muertos Petaluma, Bolca Avia, Chelsea Antiques, Café Puente, Rustic Bakery, Quality Inn Petaluma, and all of the organizations, volunteers, artists, and community members whose collaboration has brought this exhibition to life.

title: Debashish Bhattacharya
location: HopMonk Tavern
description:
Born in Kolkata in 1963 into a family of vocalists, by age 4 Pandit Debashish Bhattacharya had already learned to play classical Indian ragas on the Hawaiian lap steel slide guitar, making his debut on All India Radio. After further training with family, at age 21, when most artists in the field would normally start promoting themselves, he chose instead to take on a 10-year period of rigorous and highly disciplined training with the great teacher Pandit Brij Bhashan Kabra, the pioneer of Indian classical guitar. During this time, he made no public performances, but developed a deep understanding of traditional music and a simply mind-boggling technical skill. Emerging from these years of hardship came a unique vision that not only preserves the classical tradition but extends it into newly imagined forms and colors. 

Critical to carrying out this vision are the unique instruments that he designs and manufactures. He has invented a number of slide guitars, uniquely adapted to his music including the 24-string Chaturangui, the 23-string Pushpa Veena, the 14-string Gandharvi, and the 4-string Anandi. 

Bhattacharya has received numerous awards and accolades, whose highlights include the President of India Gold Medal in 1994, a Grammy nomination, Billboard Magazine’s Top 10 world music recordings, Songlines Magazine’s Top 10 recordings and the BBC Planet Award. His 2018 album “Hawaii to Kolkata: a Tribute to Tau Mo” was \#3 in “50 Greatest World Music Albums of the Last Five Years” published by Songlines Magazine in the UK.  

Bhattacharya’s devotees and recording collaborators include John McLaughlin, Jerry Douglas, Derek Trucks, Ballake Sissoko, Lulo Reinhardt, Martin Simpson, Bob Brozman, and Zakir Hussain.

The breath specific movements stretch the diaphragm, psoas, massage the heart and internal organs, clear the lungs, drain the lymphatic system, stimulate the vagus nerve and calm the mind. Energy is created along the spine and central nervous system, and is distributed throughout the nadis and into the entire energy body. Regular practice of Talasana flowers into to ananta samapatti and understanding "stillness in movement".
Class begins with Opening Mantras & Ding Namaskar (Devotional Salutation to the Directional Spheres with Breath & Mantra). Then moves to Tāĺāsana to Savasana then Seated Prānāyāma (Yogic Breathing) including Morning Cleansing Kriyas, Ujjayi, Nadi Shuddi, Samantraka Prānāyāma, Pratyahara, Dharana. title: Henry Frank: J-80928: A Human Experience Exhibition
location: San Geronimo Valley Community Center
description:
The San Geronimo Valley Community Center is proud to present featured September artist **Henry Frank** in the Del Mue Galleries this September. There will be a reception for the artist as part of the International Day of Peace Festival Finale on **September 20 from 2 – 6 pm**.

**J-80928: A Human Experience Exhibition** explores Henry Frank’s transformative journey through nearly three decades of incarceration in the California Department of Corrections. Through deeply personal artwork, the exhibition reflects on trauma, friendship, identity, hope, and personal growth while inviting viewers to recognize the humanity and capacity for change in people who are incarcerated.

**ARTISTS STATEMENT** **J-80928: A Human Experience Exhibition** explores my personal journey serving a 29-year-to-life sentence in the California Department of Corrections as an Indigenous person, an artist, and a human being. I was incarcerated from February 15, 1994, to April 19, 2013, and during much of that time, I lived hour to hour. For the first 14 years, my mantras were: expect the worst and hope for the best, trust no one except myself, and fear is a state of mind. While many experiences were deeply traumatic, there were also moments of humanity, compassion, joy, and empathy that transformed how I saw myself and the world around me.

The last six years of my incarceration became the most transformative period of my life. I began to believe that I would not die in prison. I found hope, discovered the importance of serving others, began to see myself as a serious artist, and gained a deeper understanding of my place in the world. My mantras evolved into: expect the best and be prepared for anything less, trust everyone until they give me a reason not to, and happiness is a choice. During this time, I learned to love and respect myself, to be accountable, to live in the present, to be a true friend, and to serve others with intention and compassion.

This exhibition is an oeuvre dedicated to the experiences, emotional trauma, friendships, and reclamation of identity that shaped me throughout my incarceration. Through this body of work, I hope people can connect with parts of my journey and recognize that I am not so different from them. More importantly, I want to humanize those who are currently incarcerated and raise awareness that people are capable of change. They can become contributing members of their communities. They have families, hobbies, hopes, dreams, and the capacity for growth and transformation.

I have been working toward completing this body of work and plan to have the exhibition finished completely by the end of this year.

This exhibition is partially funded by an Artist Fellowship Grant from the Art for Justice Fund. I am grateful for their support and patience for this exhibition to evolve into its fullest potential.

Human Being

Henry Edward Frank

Yurok and Kashaya Pomo

description:
Regenerative Ayurvedic Yoga with Tirza Dawn
Come, step onto your mat with an open heart and an open mind.
Invest in your self care and join us for morning yoga in the OCA studio. $20 per class, $15 for OCA members. Yoga is offered Mondays from 10-11:10 AM and also on Wednesdays from 8:30-9:40 AM. The registration below is for Mondays.
Pay at the door for a-la-carte sessions or use the links below to pay ahead for four weeks at a time.
Pay Online 4 sessions
Tirza Dawn Naramore
is a yogi, mother, artist, ceremonialist and lover of life. She has been practicing and teaching yoga and meditation for 30 years and offers yoga retreats and trainings that center on optimum health, self realization and self love. Her teachers are from many yoga and tantric traditions, but her primary lineages are Iyengar and Kali Ray.
Tirza is deeply devoted to community building and is honored to have created a number of community supported non profits including Mystic Family Circus and The AWAKEN Project, which serves families with children on the autism spectrum. Tirza is proud to be the mother of 3 wild teenagers, including her incredible son who is diagnosed with autism.
Tirza’s spirituality is one of many influences and teachings. Beginning with a Christian up-bringing and being raised on a Christian commune in her early childhood, she later expanded into more earth-based ways. While in her 20’s Tirza was adopted into the Native American Church, where she learned from her relatives a way of living the “Beauty Way.”
During the 1990’s and early 2000’s, Tirza lived in San Francisco, Oakland and Berkeley, directing the Mystic Family Circus, which was a performance group dedicated to cultural awareness and bridge building. She worked with Cirque du Soleil, Burning Man, Reclaiming, Contraband, CELLspace and other Bay Area art collectives and non profits to provide conscious entertainment and “prayerformances” for the betterment of humankind and the planet.
In 2012, Tirza helped to found the Buckeye Gathering, an ancestral skills gathering in Northern California which draws teachers and students of all ages to learn ancestral ways of tending the earth and survival skills.
Tirza Dawn was the founder of yoga programming and the Ayurvedic Yoga Teacher Trainings at the dhyana Center of Ayurveda in Sebastopol, California, which operated a community center of healing and education from 2010 to 2020.

title: Art Exhibit: Painting in Fauve
location: Upstairs Art Gallery
description:
Date: FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE  7/15/26

AUGUST EXHIBIT: PAINTING IN FAUVE

EXHIBIT DATES:  July 27 – August 30, 2026

RECEPTION: SATURDAY, August 1, 2026, 3-6 pm: Join us to meet Willow LaLand and Gen Zorich;  Learn about their art and celebrate the show.  Be sure to take part in the Gallery’s free monthlong drawing for a beautiful work by a Gallery artist.  Refreshments will be served.

Sonoma wine country artist, Willow LaLand presents Painting in Fauve, a collection of oil and acrylic paintings focusing on our region’s vibrant beauty through the artist’s Fauvist lens.  Known for her hyper-realistic landscapes, these works take an imaginative turn to the fantastical, tapping into the wild Fauve vivid color palette.   Highlighting the show, “Mt. Tamalpais” comes alive, swathed in rich colors cascading over its undulating slopes, while rich foreground purple/blues heighten the mountain’s grandeur.  “Fitch Mountain” similarly seems to sing with color as it overlooks a lush vineyard.  LaLand’s color lens takes us from palette to palate as she captures the luxuriant purple/reds of a fine red wine in “Sommelier’s Dream.”  Reflecting on her creative process, LaLand notes “I love the artistic freedom to play, create depth in color, and give a tangible realistic impression within a completely fantastical expression.”

A third-generation artist, LaLand started her studies as a young girl and had a studio space at 10 years old.  She is inspired by early American realists and uses traditional techniques to achieve dramatic realism.  LaLand finds the Fauve color palette elicits a joyful response to her themes of nature and wine.  Many of her collectors love both her styles and have a hard time, though they vastly differ, choosing between the two.  LaLand exhibits widely, including internationally, and participated in the Art Trails Program.  She was featured in American Art Collector magazine in 2013 and on KRCB in 2015.

Meet the artist: LaLand will host the Gallery on August 2, 2:30 – 6pm and August 16 & 29, 11am to 6 pm.

The Stairway Smallworks Showcase features Gen Zorich’s Summertime, highlighting the beauty of wine country and the warmth of long, lazy summer days.  From Zorich’s background as a geologist and environmental scientist, she imbues her paintings with a deep understanding of the natural world. Focusing on flora, pink waterlilies floating on pastel pads in “Summer Color” engender a sense of sun-filled easy days.  These works would bring a feeling of summer contentment any time of year.  An award-winning artist, Zorich has exhibited widely and has been a longtime participant in the Sonoma County Art Trails Program.

Meet the artist: Zorich will host the Gallery on August 2, 11am – 2:30pm, August 4, 11am to 6 pm and August 21 & 23, 2:30 – 6pm.

Also join us for ART NITE HEALDSBURG, Thursday, August 6, 5 – 7 pm.  ART NITE Healdsburg, held the 1st Thursday of Every Month, is a community event celebrating art and creativity with over 20 galleries participating. This month’s special theme: Music and Mocktails.  ArtNiteHealdsburg.com.

Upstairs Art Gallery, 306 Center Street, Healdsburg, CA 95448. \(707\) 431-4214.: OPEN DAILY: 11am – 6 pm.    www.upstairsart gallery.net 

For further information: Contact: Beverly Bird, Press Contact, at bvdrio@sonic.net or 707-799-1490.

title: ART EXHIBIT:  THE DAYS OF VINES AND ROSES
location: Upstairs Art Gallery
description:
EPTEMBER ART EXHIBIT:  THE DAYS OF VINES AND ROSES

Date: FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE  8/12/26

DATES: August 31 – September 27, 2026

RECEPTION:  SATURDAY, September 5 – 3 -6 pm Join Donna Schaffer and Tosya Shore to celebrate the show and learn about their artistic inspirations.  Refreshments will be served.  

Featured Artist Donna Schaffer Celebrates Wine Country Beauty in “The Days of Vines and Roses”

Sonoma County artist Donna Schaffer unveils her latest collection of oil paintings, “The Days of Vines and Roses,” celebrating some of her favorite views of roses blooming among the vineyards, hills, and woodlands of Sonoma County. At the heart of the collection is Vines and Trellis of Roses, where glorious pink roses spill across an entrance trellis, set against the orderly rows of a vineyard. In Mini Red Roses Along Vineyard, delicate red roses punctuate the landscape, creating a lively interplay between vineyard rows, stands of trees, and the hills beyond. “Living here in Sonoma County for three decades, I never tire of its glorious natural beauty. It is an enduring inspiration and truly a painter’s dream,” says Schaffer.

Art has been a focus throughout Schaffer’s life. She has been painting full time in Dry Creek since the mid-1990s and is particularly known for her paintings of Sonoma County’s wine country. Her work are popular with both locals and visitors who want to bring a bit of Sonoma’s beauty and magic into their own homes. Schaffer has been a member of the Upstairs Art Gallery for more than 25 years and has exhibited regionally, including eight years as an Art Trails artist.

Meet the artist:  Schaffer will be hosting the Gallery on September 3 and 27 from 11-6 pm.  

Stairway Showcase: Tosya Shore — “It’s Black and White with a Splash of Color”

The Stairway Showcase presents artist Tosya Shore’s “It’s Black and White with a Splash of Color,” a collection of watercolors that begins with the fundamentals of composition: reducing an image to its two most essential elements—black and white. Working with ink, a stick, and a scraper, Shore roughens the edges of her subjects and strips away unnecessary detail, allowing light itself—not form or precision—to take center stage. Her paintings invite the viewer to experience the essence of a scene through contrast, gesture, and the expressive qualities of the medium.

In addition to her watercolor works, Shore presents paintings inspired by a recent trip to Carmel, where she picked up oil paint for the first time and explored painting the ocean using nothing but a palette knife. The resulting works introduce a vibrant splash of color and texture into a practice grounded in restraint—new pigment, new surface, yet the same enduring fascination with light over likeness.

title: Salsa Beginners 2 - Mondays
location: Salsa Dance Marin
description:
Ready to take your salsa to the next level? Salsa lessons in Marin will help you to add some flair and fluidity to your salsa dancing.

Pre-requisite: Salsa Beginners 1 – You know your basic steps, left turn, right turn, cross-body lead, and you hold your frame.

What You’ll Learn

We’ve curated a curriculum designed to build your confidence and your “social dance” vocabulary:

• The Cross Body Lead \(CBL\) Series: Master both Inside and Outside Turns, the essential building blocks for moving your partner across the floor with grace.

• The “I Turn – You Turn”: A classic social dance staple that develops timing and hand-change coordination.

• The Walk-Through: Learn how to transition smoothly through the dance space without breaking your rhythm.

• Footwork & Shine: We’ll break down the footwork pattern that adds personality to your “shines.”

Technique & Artistry

• Dancing is about more than just where your feet go. In this level, we dive deeper into the “how”:

• The Frame: Understand the “tension and compression” needed to lead and follow clearly without using muscle.

• Upper Body Mechanics: Learn how to isolate your ribcage and shoulders to move with that authentic Latin soul.

• Connection: Developing a “heavy” but responsive arm connection to ensure your partner feels every lead.

Important Details

• No dance experience required: Whether you’ve never danced before or it’s been a while, you’re welcome here!

• No partner necessary: Come solo or bring a friend—either way, you’ll have plenty of opportunities to dance.

• Please wear non-marking shoe soles: This helps us keep our dance floor in great condition.

title: Stories We Carry
location: Petaluma Historical Library and Museum
description:
Every object has a story. Meet the people behind them. 

Multiple Dates: September 12 & 19, 6-8 pm

Petaluma Historical Library & Museum

20 4th Street \(Corner of 4th & B Street\)

Free Admission, Light refreshments will be served.

RSVP is recommended.

Join us for two special evenings with the community storytellers featured in Belongings: What We Bring, What We Leave Behind. Through family heirlooms, treasured keepsakes, photographs, letters, and everyday belongings, participants will share the deeply personal stories that bring the exhibition to life. 

Hear firsthand reflections on migration, identity, resilience, family, and the meaning of home. These intimate conversations offer a rare opportunity to connect directly with the individuals whose voices and objects are featured throughout the exhibition, creating space for dialogue, empathy, and shared understanding. 

Following the storytelling program, continue the conversation while exploring the exhibition and enjoying light refreshments. 

Stories We Carry is presented as part of Belongings: What We Bring, What We Leave Behind, on view September 4–October 4, 2026, at the Petaluma Historical Library & Museum. The exhibition explores migration, memory, and belonging through the meaningful objects and personal stories that connect us across generations and cultures. 

Belongings: What We Bring, What We Leave Behind is made possible through the generous support of California Humanities through its Connecting California grant program. We are also deeply grateful to our community partners and sponsors, including the North Bay Asian American Pacific Islander Coalition, Sonoma County Japanese American Citizens League, Petaluma Arts Center, Life on Art, Zimbabwe Cultural Exchange Project of California, El Día de los Muertos Petaluma, Bolca Avia, Chelsea Antiques, Café Puente, Rustic Bakery, Quality Inn Petaluma, and all of the organizations, volunteers, artists, and community members whose collaboration has brought this exhibition to life.

title: Lavender Labyrinth Sound Bath Experience
location: Bees n blooms
description:
Join us in our most dreamy location yet, in the center of a lavender labyrinth for an exquisite sunset sound Bath Experience!

Join us in our most dreamy location yet, in the middle of lavender labyrinth at sunset!

Mondays through October 6th

We are thrilled to share this magic with you! Let the fragrance of lavender fill and sooth your senses as the sound expands your awareness.

Sound baths create the space for self-healing and transformation. The resonance of the instruments is not just an auditory experience ~ it's like receiving a full body sound massage.

There will be 8 Gongs, Crystal singing bowls, Hand pan, Mono chord, Chimes galore, Ocean drum, Native drum, Angelic Vocals & more.The vibrations will transport you on a powerful healing journey!

PLEASE NOTE: The sound bath starts at 7pm. Gates close at 6:45 PM. Please be Mindful of timing. You will need time to park, walk up and set up. You are welcome to come walk the labyrinth and visit the Farm Stand from 6 pm onward. Please check the hourly weather so you are prepaired. You will be lying on the grass, so please bring all that you will need to feel cozy and warm, "yoga mat" or camping pad, "Blanket" or sleeping bag, a pillow, eye mask, and water bottle. Wonderful Lavender Eye Masks will be available to purchase for $25 by the Bees & Blooms Farm Stand.

If we have environmental Circumstance such as rain or unhealthy air quality due to fires we will postpone to Wednesday of the same week and your tickets will roll over to that day. If these conditions are present it is your responsibility to monitor your emails\(also junk/spam\) for notifications. In these force of nature situations Tickets are not refundable but are transferable! Your understanding and cooperation is greatly appreciated.

Please be informed that there are bee hives on site and there may be bees on the lavender plants. If you are allergic to bee stings, bring your Epipen. An incident is unlikely, but best to be prepared. Also, at some point, probably mid July the Lavender will began to be harvested so there may be less lavender towards the end of the month.Full Bloom occurs mid June. The last sound bath of the Lavender season will be Oct. 6th. The labyrinth & farm will be beautiful however the Lavender will be reaching the end of its cycle around mid. July. You will walk through many rows of a varity of blooming flowers on you way from parking.

Only disability trained Registered Service dogs are permitted because of the animals on the farm and the nature of the Sound Bath. Your understanding is appreciated. Also, please no children under 10 years of age.

Labyrinths represent a metaphor for your life path and the journey you are making. While walking the path of the labyrinth, either alone or with a group, focus on your feelings and emotions to allow you to connect with yourself. You may also want to choose a meditation that you are comfortable with in order to clear and quiet your mind. The uses of a labyrinth are many; relief from stress and anxiety, healing, meditation, problem solving, enhancing intuition, expanding thought processes, communicating with the Divine, balancing mind, body and spirit, letting go of unwanted energies, obtaining goals, celebrating and remembering others, building trust in yourself or others, and coping with grief, sorrow and loss. The labyrinth is an ancient symbol that relates to wholeness. It combines the imagery of the circle and the spiral into a meandering but purposeful path. The Labyrinth represents a journey to our own center and back again out into the world. Labyrinths have long been used as meditation and prayer tools.

Looking forward to sharing this Extraordinary Experience with you! In Gratitude

title: Tom Chown: 46 Years Behind the Lens
location: Robert F. Agrella Art Gallery - Santa Rosa Campus
description: Santa Rosa Junior College will celebrate the 46-year career of longtime staff photographer Tom Chown with a photography exhibition featuring images from his decades at the college, from the days of film and darkrooms to the digital era.  Chown began his career at SRJC at age 24, working in the campus photography lab. Over the next 46 years, he became a familiar presence throughout the college community, documenting the people, programs and milestones that shaped generations of students and employees.  The exhibition will trace Chown's evolution as a photographer, from working with film and developing photographs in the darkroom to embracing digital photography. It also offers a visual history of SRJC, preserving moments from nearly five decades of college life.  The exhibition is free and open to the public.Location: Robert F. Agrella Art Gallery, Doyle Library 1st floor - Santa Rosa CampusFor more information, visit SRJC's Robert F. Agrella Art Gallery website. College Ave., Santa Rosa, CA. The show is free and open to the public Monday – Friday, 8:30 a.m.-4:30 p.m., through November 19.

The established and up-and-coming native artists create with digital media, paint and traditional materials in their art, weaving, regalia, beadwork, jewelry, baskets and quilts. The artists include:

·         Meyo Marrufo, painter, guest curator for the de Young Museum and the Sonoma Valley Art Museum,

·         Buffie Campbell, Vice Chair, Sherwood Valley Rancheria, cultural teacher and master basket maker,

·         Henry Edward Frank, Yurok/Kashaya Pomo, who will show paintings and work with Legos titled Mind Prison,

·         Digital artist Nicolas \(Nico\) Vargas, Kashia Band of Pomo Indians, whose art was featured at the 55th Annual Stanford Powwow.

·         plus Gloria Carretero; Rose Hammock; Rudy Hammock; Jocelyn Garcia; Arella Ortega LaRose, Kashia Band of Pomo Indians; Angelica Smith, Manchester Point Arena and Yokayo Rancheria; Maria Pasalo; Michelle Napoli; Martina Morgan, Kashia Band of Pomo Indians; Hands Lopez; Shashoni Hanover-Redenbaugh; Katie Williams-Elliott, Juan Partida, and Mia Pasalo, Big Valley Pomo Tribe.

\*\*RSVP ONLY - \*Certain injuries & health issues may be contraindicated - Please contact me if you have a concern \*\*\*

Start your morning with traditional yogic breathwork with the added benefits of sunshine, fresh air and grounding. It is ideal to practice pranayama outside.

Pranayama is distinct from modern breathwork. It is an important component & taught in context to the process of yoga. Designed to harness prana (life force energy), purify & balance the nadis (channels) & awaken subtle energy for physical, mental, and spiritual development. Not limited to just well-being. Not a quick fix or forceful temporary cathartic experiences, but taught as a safe & gradual process requiring discipline & consistency.

Release toxins, clear and align the energy channels, strengthen the lungs, massage, tone & nourish internal organs, strengthen agni & digestion, oxygenate and improve blood flow, strengthen immunity & clear the mind. Known to increase neuroplasticity, nitric oxide, and erase old mental and emotional patterns. Traditionally, pranayama is the doorway to access higher states of consciousness.

Throughout the ongoing class different practices will be presented. Learn Cleansing kriyas, Himalayan Pranayama including including Ujjayi Variations, Heating & Cooling Breaths, Solar, Lunar & Soli-Lunar Nadi Shuddhi practices, Samantraka Pranayama, Mudra, Pratyahara, Subtle & Contemplative Practices. Includes Pranava techniques for contemplation and merging with the vibration and sound of Om and Nada - internal sound current.

Kara is a long time practitioner & teacher- trained extensively with Himalayan yoga adepts in advanced pranayama & mudra using the breath as the guide for transformation and self-empowerment. With deep knowledge of pranayama, she safely guides practitioners progressively.

The San Geronimo Valley Community Center is proud to present featured September artist **Henry Frank** in the Del Mue Galleries this September. There will be a reception for the artist as part of the International Day of Peace Festival Finale on **September 20 from 2 – 6 pm**.

**J-80928: A Human Experience Exhibition** explores Henry Frank’s transformative journey through nearly three decades of incarceration in the California Department of Corrections. Through deeply personal artwork, the exhibition reflects on trauma, friendship, identity, hope, and personal growth while inviting viewers to recognize the humanity and capacity for change in people who are incarcerated.

**ARTISTS STATEMENT** **J-80928: A Human Experience Exhibition** explores my personal journey serving a 29-year-to-life sentence in the California Department of Corrections as an Indigenous person, an artist, and a human being. I was incarcerated from February 15, 1994, to April 19, 2013, and during much of that time, I lived hour to hour. For the first 14 years, my mantras were: expect the worst and hope for the best, trust no one except myself, and fear is a state of mind. While many experiences were deeply traumatic, there were also moments of humanity, compassion, joy, and empathy that transformed how I saw myself and the world around me.

The last six years of my incarceration became the most transformative period of my life. I began to believe that I would not die in prison. I found hope, discovered the importance of serving others, began to see myself as a serious artist, and gained a deeper understanding of my place in the world. My mantras evolved into: expect the best and be prepared for anything less, trust everyone until they give me a reason not to, and happiness is a choice. During this time, I learned to love and respect myself, to be accountable, to live in the present, to be a true friend, and to serve others with intention and compassion.

This exhibition is an oeuvre dedicated to the experiences, emotional trauma, friendships, and reclamation of identity that shaped me throughout my incarceration. Through this body of work, I hope people can connect with parts of my journey and recognize that I am not so different from them. More importantly, I want to humanize those who are currently incarcerated and raise awareness that people are capable of change. They can become contributing members of their communities. They have families, hobbies, hopes, dreams, and the capacity for growth and transformation.

I have been working toward completing this body of work and plan to have the exhibition finished completely by the end of this year.

This exhibition is partially funded by an Artist Fellowship Grant from the Art for Justice Fund. I am grateful for their support and patience for this exhibition to evolve into its fullest potential.

Human Being

Henry Edward Frank

Yurok and Kashaya Pomo

title: Watercolor | Building Technique II, with Nancy Ballard
location: Petaluma Arts Center
description:
Building on the skills and confidence you developed in the first class, this watercolor workshop invites you to take your ideas a step further. Explore how a simple sketch, thoughtful composition, and expressive use of color can transform an idea into a finished painting.

We'll work larger and bolder while exploring watercolor techniques including:

Wet-on-wet paintingLoose interpretation and expressive mark-makingCreating shadows and depthEnhancing backgroundsWorking in black and whiteExploring the many variations and possibilities of mixing greens

Bring a favorite photograph, a live flower or small plant, or even a meaningful memory to use as inspiration. No matter where you are in your artistic journey, you'll be encouraged to experiment, have fun, and focus on the larger picture rather than striving for perfection. There are no mistakes in art—only opportunities to explore.

Please Note: There will be a $10 supply fee paid directly to the Nancy on the day of the class.

Nancy's classes sell out quickly and we only 16 spots available, so reserve your spot now!

 If you've taken Nancy's Gentle Watercolor workshop, this class will build on the skills and techniques you've already developed. If you're new to the series, you'll find a welcoming, supportive environment where you can jump right in. All experience levels are welcome, and you'll be guided along the way.

Nancy Ballard's love of art began in childhood, when she first discovered the magic of brush and paint—a sense of wonder that continues to shape her work today. After a full life as a mother, grandmother, and corporate professional, she returned to art following her retirement in 2006, studying watercolor with Mary L. Harden at Strybing Arboretum. In 2009, she was recognized as a Master Artist of Botanical Illustration by the San Francisco Botanical Garden Society. Nancy has also worked as a gallery curator and exhibiting artist throughout the Bay Area, sharing her botanical work in galleries, wineries, hospitals, and nonprofit spaces while supporting environmental awareness through art.

title: Art Exhibit: Painting in Fauve
location: Upstairs Art Gallery
description:
Date: FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE  7/15/26

AUGUST EXHIBIT: PAINTING IN FAUVE

EXHIBIT DATES:  July 27 – August 30, 2026

RECEPTION: SATURDAY, August 1, 2026, 3-6 pm: Join us to meet Willow LaLand and Gen Zorich;  Learn about their art and celebrate the show.  Be sure to take part in the Gallery’s free monthlong drawing for a beautiful work by a Gallery artist.  Refreshments will be served.

Sonoma wine country artist, Willow LaLand presents Painting in Fauve, a collection of oil and acrylic paintings focusing on our region’s vibrant beauty through the artist’s Fauvist lens.  Known for her hyper-realistic landscapes, these works take an imaginative turn to the fantastical, tapping into the wild Fauve vivid color palette.   Highlighting the show, “Mt. Tamalpais” comes alive, swathed in rich colors cascading over its undulating slopes, while rich foreground purple/blues heighten the mountain’s grandeur.  “Fitch Mountain” similarly seems to sing with color as it overlooks a lush vineyard.  LaLand’s color lens takes us from palette to palate as she captures the luxuriant purple/reds of a fine red wine in “Sommelier’s Dream.”  Reflecting on her creative process, LaLand notes “I love the artistic freedom to play, create depth in color, and give a tangible realistic impression within a completely fantastical expression.”

A third-generation artist, LaLand started her studies as a young girl and had a studio space at 10 years old.  She is inspired by early American realists and uses traditional techniques to achieve dramatic realism.  LaLand finds the Fauve color palette elicits a joyful response to her themes of nature and wine.  Many of her collectors love both her styles and have a hard time, though they vastly differ, choosing between the two.  LaLand exhibits widely, including internationally, and participated in the Art Trails Program.  She was featured in American Art Collector magazine in 2013 and on KRCB in 2015.

Meet the artist: LaLand will host the Gallery on August 2, 2:30 – 6pm and August 16 & 29, 11am to 6 pm.

The Stairway Smallworks Showcase features Gen Zorich’s Summertime, highlighting the beauty of wine country and the warmth of long, lazy summer days.  From Zorich’s background as a geologist and environmental scientist, she imbues her paintings with a deep understanding of the natural world. Focusing on flora, pink waterlilies floating on pastel pads in “Summer Color” engender a sense of sun-filled easy days.  These works would bring a feeling of summer contentment any time of year.  An award-winning artist, Zorich has exhibited widely and has been a longtime participant in the Sonoma County Art Trails Program.

Meet the artist: Zorich will host the Gallery on August 2, 11am – 2:30pm, August 4, 11am to 6 pm and August 21 & 23, 2:30 – 6pm.

Also join us for ART NITE HEALDSBURG, Thursday, August 6, 5 – 7 pm.  ART NITE Healdsburg, held the 1st Thursday of Every Month, is a community event celebrating art and creativity with over 20 galleries participating. This month’s special theme: Music and Mocktails.  ArtNiteHealdsburg.com.

For further information: Contact: Beverly Bird, Press Contact, at bvdrio@sonic.net or 707-799-1490.

title: ART EXHIBIT:  THE DAYS OF VINES AND ROSES
location: Upstairs Art Gallery
description:
EPTEMBER ART EXHIBIT:  THE DAYS OF VINES AND ROSES

Date: FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE  8/12/26

DATES: August 31 – September 27, 2026

RECEPTION:  SATURDAY, September 5 – 3 -6 pm Join Donna Schaffer and Tosya Shore to celebrate the show and learn about their artistic inspirations.  Refreshments will be served.  

Featured Artist Donna Schaffer Celebrates Wine Country Beauty in “The Days of Vines and Roses”

Sonoma County artist Donna Schaffer unveils her latest collection of oil paintings, “The Days of Vines and Roses,” celebrating some of her favorite views of roses blooming among the vineyards, hills, and woodlands of Sonoma County. At the heart of the collection is Vines and Trellis of Roses, where glorious pink roses spill across an entrance trellis, set against the orderly rows of a vineyard. In Mini Red Roses Along Vineyard, delicate red roses punctuate the landscape, creating a lively interplay between vineyard rows, stands of trees, and the hills beyond. “Living here in Sonoma County for three decades, I never tire of its glorious natural beauty. It is an enduring inspiration and truly a painter’s dream,” says Schaffer.

Art has been a focus throughout Schaffer’s life. She has been painting full time in Dry Creek since the mid-1990s and is particularly known for her paintings of Sonoma County’s wine country. Her work are popular with both locals and visitors who want to bring a bit of Sonoma’s beauty and magic into their own homes. Schaffer has been a member of the Upstairs Art Gallery for more than 25 years and has exhibited regionally, including eight years as an Art Trails artist.

Meet the artist:  Schaffer will be hosting the Gallery on September 3 and 27 from 11-6 pm.  

Stairway Showcase: Tosya Shore — “It’s Black and White with a Splash of Color”

The Stairway Showcase presents artist Tosya Shore’s “It’s Black and White with a Splash of Color,” a collection of watercolors that begins with the fundamentals of composition: reducing an image to its two most essential elements—black and white. Working with ink, a stick, and a scraper, Shore roughens the edges of her subjects and strips away unnecessary detail, allowing light itself—not form or precision—to take center stage. Her paintings invite the viewer to experience the essence of a scene through contrast, gesture, and the expressive qualities of the medium.

In addition to her watercolor works, Shore presents paintings inspired by a recent trip to Carmel, where she picked up oil paint for the first time and explored painting the ocean using nothing but a palette knife. The resulting works introduce a vibrant splash of color and texture into a practice grounded in restraint—new pigment, new surface, yet the same enduring fascination with light over likeness.

From an Oscar, Peabody, and Emmy award-winning team, “The Stamp Thief” is part detective story, part heist film, and part untold history. The documentary investigates a tale dating back to the Holocaust: that a mysterious Nazi stole priceless stamp collections from concentration camp victims and buried the stolen stamps in a small town in Poland.

Embarking on a real-life “Argo”-like adventure, one-time “Seinfeld” producer Gary Gilbert sets out to confirm the story and recover the stamps. His tactic: a fake movie shoot. His goal: to return the stamps to their rightful owners, hopefully delivering a small measure of justice more than 70 years after the Holocaust.

title: Stories We Carry
location: Petaluma Historical Library and Museum
description:
Every object has a story. Meet the people behind them. 

Multiple Dates: September 12 & 19, 6-8 pm

Petaluma Historical Library & Museum

20 4th Street \(Corner of 4th & B Street\)

Free Admission, Light refreshments will be served.

RSVP is recommended.

Join us for two special evenings with the community storytellers featured in Belongings: What We Bring, What We Leave Behind. Through family heirlooms, treasured keepsakes, photographs, letters, and everyday belongings, participants will share the deeply personal stories that bring the exhibition to life. 

Hear firsthand reflections on migration, identity, resilience, family, and the meaning of home. These intimate conversations offer a rare opportunity to connect directly with the individuals whose voices and objects are featured throughout the exhibition, creating space for dialogue, empathy, and shared understanding. 

Following the storytelling program, continue the conversation while exploring the exhibition and enjoying light refreshments. 

Stories We Carry is presented as part of Belongings: What We Bring, What We Leave Behind, on view September 4–October 4, 2026, at the Petaluma Historical Library & Museum. The exhibition explores migration, memory, and belonging through the meaningful objects and personal stories that connect us across generations and cultures. 

Belongings: What We Bring, What We Leave Behind is made possible through the generous support of California Humanities through its Connecting California grant program. We are also deeply grateful to our community partners and sponsors, including the North Bay Asian American Pacific Islander Coalition, Sonoma County Japanese American Citizens League, Petaluma Arts Center, Life on Art, Zimbabwe Cultural Exchange Project of California, El Día de los Muertos Petaluma, Bolca Avia, Chelsea Antiques, Café Puente, Rustic Bakery, Quality Inn Petaluma, and all of the organizations, volunteers, artists, and community members whose collaboration has brought this exhibition to life.
