title: Artist's Way Group Next Chapter: "The Book of Alchemy"
location: Alibi Bookshop
description: Creativity is my way of making sense of the world.” — Suleika Jaouad  Are you feeling an urge to pick up a pen or paintbrush or pair of scissors and unleash your creativity, but not sure where to start? Or are you looking to find community, to motivate your creative self and make new friends? This might be just the thing for you. Two years ago, we formed an “Artist’s Way” group here at the shop, and continued it again last year. It was extraordinary. Not only did people write and paint and create, but got published and found new life paths. \(And even love!\) But best of all, a community was established, offering encouragement for creative endeavors, and friendship and support. It has been life affirming. Now, in 2026, creativity and community are more important than ever, and it’s time to gather a group again! This year, however, we will not be doing “The Artist’s Way,” and instead will be exploring “The Book of Alchemy” by Suleika Jaouad. This book focuses on journaling and looking at our life experiences to foster creativity to inspire whatever art form we choose to do.  From the publisher: “From the time she was young, Suleika Jaouad has kept a journal. She’s used it to mark life’s biggest occasions and to weather its most ferocious storms. Journaling has buoyed her through illness, heartbreak, and the deepest uncertainty. And she is not alone: for so many people, keeping a journal is an essential tool for navigating both the personal peaks and valleys and the collective challenges of modern life. More than ever, we need a space for puzzling through. In The Book of Alchemy, Suleika explores the art of journaling and shares everything she’s learned about how this life-altering practice can help us tap into that mystical trait that exists in every human: creativity. She has gathered wisdom from one hundred writers, artists, and thinkers in the form of essays and writing prompts. Their insights invite us to inhabit a more inspired life. A companion through challenging times, The Book of Alchemy is broken into themes ranging from new beginnings to love, loss, and rebuilding. Whether you’re a lifelong journaler or new to the practice, this book gives you the tools, direction, and encouragement to engage with discomfort, ask questions, peel back the layers, dream daringly, uncover your truest self—and in doing so, to learn to hold the unbearably brutal and astonishingly beautiful facts of life in the same palm.” Beginning Tuesday, March 3rd at 7pm through the end of September \(with flexibility\), we will be meeting on Tuesdays to check in and discuss the book and our progress. Each chapter has a number of prompts so we will take it slow, but also determine our pace. Every other Tuesday we will discuss the book, and then the alternate weeks will be more open — we can listen to chapters or inspiring podcasts while crafting, or just get together and talk — to give people a chance to catch up or take some time. The initial meeting on March 3rd is a welcome meeting for introductions, to pick up the book, and to set some intentions— no need to read anything yet. The cost is $40 plus the purchase of the book.  To register, come by the shop or email alibibookshop@gmail.com. Registration “closes” the end of March.  This group is truly one of the best things I have ever been a part of, and I’m looking forward to doing it again— and welcoming new folks to the fold! Hope to see you!

title: The Santa Rosa Original Certified Farmers Market

description: The Santa Rosa Original Certified Farmers Market is a year-round Saturday tradition in Sonoma County, bringing together local farmers, ranchers, food artisans, and neighbors from 8:30 a.m. to 1 p.m. This is not just a place to shop, it's a place to connect directly with the people who grow your food. As a Slow Food Sonoma County award recipient, the market prioritizes integrity, seasonality, and true farm-to-community relationships. Expect peak-season produce harvested just hours before market, pasture-raised meats, fresh flowers, artisan breads, handcrafted goods, and thoughtfully prepared foods that reflect the region's agricultural richness. Visitors can stroll the vibrant open-air market, sample local flavors, and experience Sonoma County's food culture in its most authentic form. Families, chefs, and weekend explorers alike gather here to discover what's growing now and to support small farms that keep our local food system strong. Open every Saturday, rain or shine, the Santa Rosa Original Certified Farmers Market is a cornerstone of the community and a must-visit stop for anyone wanting to taste, shop, and experience Sonoma County at its freshest.

Tirza Dawn Naramore
is a yogi, mother, artist, ceremonialist and lover of life. She has been practicing and teaching yoga and meditation for 30 years and offers yoga retreats and trainings that center on optimum health, self realization and self love. Her teachers are from many yoga and tantric traditions, but her primary lineages are Iyengar and Kali Ray.
Tirza is deeply devoted to community building and is honored to have created a number of community supported non profits including Mystic Family Circus and The AWAKEN Project, which serves families with children on the autism spectrum. Tirza is proud to be the mother of 3 wild teenagers, including her incredible son who is diagnosed with autism.
Tirza’s spirituality is one of many influences and teachings. Beginning with a Christian up-bringing and being raised on a Christian commune in her early childhood, she later expanded into more earth-based ways. While in her 20’s Tirza was adopted into the Native American Church, where she learned from her relatives a way of living the “Beauty Way.”
During the 1990’s and early 2000’s, Tirza lived in San Francisco, Oakland and Berkeley, directing the Mystic Family Circus, which was a performance group dedicated to cultural awareness and bridge building. She worked with Cirque du Soleil, Burning Man, Reclaiming, Contraband, CELLspace and other Bay Area art collectives and non profits to provide conscious entertainment and “prayerformances” for the betterment of humankind and the planet.
In 2012, Tirza helped to found the Buckeye Gathering, an ancestral skills gathering in Northern California which draws teachers and students of all ages to learn ancestral ways of tending the earth and survival skills.
Tirza Dawn was the founder of yoga programming and the Ayurvedic Yoga Teacher Trainings at the dhyana Center of Ayurveda in Sebastopol, California, which operated a community center of healing and education from 2010 to 2020.

title: Henry Frank: J-80928: A Human Experience Exhibition
location: San Geronimo Valley Community Center
description:
The San Geronimo Valley Community Center is proud to present featured September artist **Henry Frank** in the Del Mue Galleries this September. There will be a reception for the artist as part of the International Day of Peace Festival Finale on **September 20 from 2 – 6 pm**.

**J-80928: A Human Experience Exhibition** explores Henry Frank’s transformative journey through nearly three decades of incarceration in the California Department of Corrections. Through deeply personal artwork, the exhibition reflects on trauma, friendship, identity, hope, and personal growth while inviting viewers to recognize the humanity and capacity for change in people who are incarcerated.

**ARTISTS STATEMENT** **J-80928: A Human Experience Exhibition** explores my personal journey serving a 29-year-to-life sentence in the California Department of Corrections as an Indigenous person, an artist, and a human being. I was incarcerated from February 15, 1994, to April 19, 2013, and during much of that time, I lived hour to hour. For the first 14 years, my mantras were: expect the worst and hope for the best, trust no one except myself, and fear is a state of mind. While many experiences were deeply traumatic, there were also moments of humanity, compassion, joy, and empathy that transformed how I saw myself and the world around me.

The last six years of my incarceration became the most transformative period of my life. I began to believe that I would not die in prison. I found hope, discovered the importance of serving others, began to see myself as a serious artist, and gained a deeper understanding of my place in the world. My mantras evolved into: expect the best and be prepared for anything less, trust everyone until they give me a reason not to, and happiness is a choice. During this time, I learned to love and respect myself, to be accountable, to live in the present, to be a true friend, and to serve others with intention and compassion.

This exhibition is an oeuvre dedicated to the experiences, emotional trauma, friendships, and reclamation of identity that shaped me throughout my incarceration. Through this body of work, I hope people can connect with parts of my journey and recognize that I am not so different from them. More importantly, I want to humanize those who are currently incarcerated and raise awareness that people are capable of change. They can become contributing members of their communities. They have families, hobbies, hopes, dreams, and the capacity for growth and transformation.

I have been working toward completing this body of work and plan to have the exhibition finished completely by the end of this year.

This exhibition is partially funded by an Artist Fellowship Grant from the Art for Justice Fund. I am grateful for their support and patience for this exhibition to evolve into its fullest potential.

Human Being

Henry Edward Frank

Yurok and Kashaya Pomo

Founded by the acclaimed team that guides renowned Pinot Noir and Chardonnay producer Rhys Vineyards, Centennial Mountain was established to explore Italian grape varieties grown on its acclaimed Centennial Mountain Vineyard in the rugged mountains of Northern Sonoma County.

The Centennial Mountain Vineyard Tasting features the winery’s coveted Nebbiolo, and the pioneering Carricante and Nerello Mascalese wines, among others. To showcase how beautifully the wines pair with food, the winery also offers a delicious Wine and Sushi Pairing from nearby Asahi Sushi, one of Healdsburg’s most popular dining destinations.

title: Art Exhibit: Painting in Fauve
location: Upstairs Art Gallery
description:
Date: FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE  7/15/26

AUGUST EXHIBIT: PAINTING IN FAUVE

EXHIBIT DATES:  July 27 – August 30, 2026

RECEPTION: SATURDAY, August 1, 2026, 3-6 pm: Join us to meet Willow LaLand and Gen Zorich;  Learn about their art and celebrate the show.  Be sure to take part in the Gallery’s free monthlong drawing for a beautiful work by a Gallery artist.  Refreshments will be served.

Sonoma wine country artist, Willow LaLand presents Painting in Fauve, a collection of oil and acrylic paintings focusing on our region’s vibrant beauty through the artist’s Fauvist lens.  Known for her hyper-realistic landscapes, these works take an imaginative turn to the fantastical, tapping into the wild Fauve vivid color palette.   Highlighting the show, “Mt. Tamalpais” comes alive, swathed in rich colors cascading over its undulating slopes, while rich foreground purple/blues heighten the mountain’s grandeur.  “Fitch Mountain” similarly seems to sing with color as it overlooks a lush vineyard.  LaLand’s color lens takes us from palette to palate as she captures the luxuriant purple/reds of a fine red wine in “Sommelier’s Dream.”  Reflecting on her creative process, LaLand notes “I love the artistic freedom to play, create depth in color, and give a tangible realistic impression within a completely fantastical expression.”

A third-generation artist, LaLand started her studies as a young girl and had a studio space at 10 years old.  She is inspired by early American realists and uses traditional techniques to achieve dramatic realism.  LaLand finds the Fauve color palette elicits a joyful response to her themes of nature and wine.  Many of her collectors love both her styles and have a hard time, though they vastly differ, choosing between the two.  LaLand exhibits widely, including internationally, and participated in the Art Trails Program.  She was featured in American Art Collector magazine in 2013 and on KRCB in 2015.

Meet the artist: LaLand will host the Gallery on August 2, 2:30 – 6pm and August 16 & 29, 11am to 6 pm.

The Stairway Smallworks Showcase features Gen Zorich’s Summertime, highlighting the beauty of wine country and the warmth of long, lazy summer days.  From Zorich’s background as a geologist and environmental scientist, she imbues her paintings with a deep understanding of the natural world. Focusing on flora, pink waterlilies floating on pastel pads in “Summer Color” engender a sense of sun-filled easy days.  These works would bring a feeling of summer contentment any time of year.  An award-winning artist, Zorich has exhibited widely and has been a longtime participant in the Sonoma County Art Trails Program.

Meet the artist: Zorich will host the Gallery on August 2, 11am – 2:30pm, August 4, 11am to 6 pm and August 21 & 23, 2:30 – 6pm.

Also join us for ART NITE HEALDSBURG, Thursday, August 6, 5 – 7 pm.  ART NITE Healdsburg, held the 1st Thursday of Every Month, is a community event celebrating art and creativity with over 20 galleries participating. This month’s special theme: Music and Mocktails.  ArtNiteHealdsburg.com.

title: ART EXHIBIT:  THE DAYS OF VINES AND ROSES
location: Upstairs Art Gallery
description:
EPTEMBER ART EXHIBIT:  THE DAYS OF VINES AND ROSES

Date: FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE  8/12/26

DATES: August 31 – September 27, 2026

RECEPTION:  SATURDAY, September 5 – 3 -6 pm Join Donna Schaffer and Tosya Shore to celebrate the show and learn about their artistic inspirations.  Refreshments will be served.  

Featured Artist Donna Schaffer Celebrates Wine Country Beauty in “The Days of Vines and Roses”

Sonoma County artist Donna Schaffer unveils her latest collection of oil paintings, “The Days of Vines and Roses,” celebrating some of her favorite views of roses blooming among the vineyards, hills, and woodlands of Sonoma County. At the heart of the collection is Vines and Trellis of Roses, where glorious pink roses spill across an entrance trellis, set against the orderly rows of a vineyard. In Mini Red Roses Along Vineyard, delicate red roses punctuate the landscape, creating a lively interplay between vineyard rows, stands of trees, and the hills beyond. “Living here in Sonoma County for three decades, I never tire of its glorious natural beauty. It is an enduring inspiration and truly a painter’s dream,” says Schaffer.

Art has been a focus throughout Schaffer’s life. She has been painting full time in Dry Creek since the mid-1990s and is particularly known for her paintings of Sonoma County’s wine country. Her work are popular with both locals and visitors who want to bring a bit of Sonoma’s beauty and magic into their own homes. Schaffer has been a member of the Upstairs Art Gallery for more than 25 years and has exhibited regionally, including eight years as an Art Trails artist.

Meet the artist:  Schaffer will be hosting the Gallery on September 3 and 27 from 11-6 pm.  

Stairway Showcase: Tosya Shore — “It’s Black and White with a Splash of Color”

The Stairway Showcase presents artist Tosya Shore’s “It’s Black and White with a Splash of Color,” a collection of watercolors that begins with the fundamentals of composition: reducing an image to its two most essential elements—black and white. Working with ink, a stick, and a scraper, Shore roughens the edges of her subjects and strips away unnecessary detail, allowing light itself—not form or precision—to take center stage. Her paintings invite the viewer to experience the essence of a scene through contrast, gesture, and the expressive qualities of the medium.

In addition to her watercolor works, Shore presents paintings inspired by a recent trip to Carmel, where she picked up oil paint for the first time and explored painting the ocean using nothing but a palette knife. The resulting works introduce a vibrant splash of color and texture into a practice grounded in restraint—new pigment, new surface, yet the same enduring fascination with light over likeness.

title: Author Talk with Vanessa Hua + Nina Schuyler
description: Join us for a special event with Vanessa Hua, author of Coyoteland, and Nina Schuyler, author of Open the Floodgates. This event is free, but we appreciate your RSVP below so we can plan for your attendance. ABOUT COYOTELAND "Coyoteland promises to be as dynamic and explosive a suburban drama as LITTLE FIRES EVERYWHERE." — LitHub | "Written with WITH, EMPATHY, and HEART." — Electric Lit | "Totally PROPULSIVE." — Ingrid Rojas Contreras | "A TOUR DE FORCE." — Kirstin Chen | "A tremendous, MESMERIZING gift." — R. O. Kwon | "UNFORGETTABLE." — J ean Kwok | "RIVETING." — Angie Kim From the BESTSELLING author of A River of Stars comes a FUNNY, HEARTFELT novel set in an affluent Bay Area suburb where a Chinese American family moves in and sets off a series of scandals. Living in El Nido, a privileged community in the hills east of Berkeley, is supposed to mean you’ve made it. So when Jin Chang moves there with his wife and daughters after years of scraping by, he hopes it will finally be the end of his bad luck. What his family doesn’t know is that he’s bending the rules for one final scheme: to make it big in real estate. Next door, Blair Belle prides herself on her progressive politics. After all, she treats their new nanny, Ana Rodriguez, and her daughter like family—even if she doesn’t know them all that well. But she can’t help but feel skeptical of the new neighbors, especially when she begins to suspect that Jin’s plans might interfere with the Belle’s own luxury development. Jin’s teenage daughter Jane can tell her dad is keeping a secret, but she’s also struggling to navigate El Nido’s cliques. Tasha Washington has always felt isolated, too, as one of the only Black girls at the school. In the wake of a coyote attack, Jane and Tasha bond. Together, they hatch a plot to expose the town’s hypocrisies. The shockwaves will rock their own families. As fire season escalates, and the roaming coyote continues to unleash chaos, the characters become embroiled in a series of scandals that will change El Nido—and their own fates—forever. Urgent, riveting, and deeply heartfelt, full of sharp wit and keen empathy, Coyoteland is at once a delicious suburban drama and an unflinching exploration of our current moment. ABOUT THE AUTHOR Vanessa Hua is the nationally-bestselling author of Coyoteland, A River of Stars, Forbidden City, and Deceit and Other Possibilities, a New York Times Editors' Pick. A National Endowment for the Arts Literature Fellow, she has received a Rona Jaffe Foundation Writers' Award, the Asian/Pacific American Award for Literature, a California Arts Council Fellowship, and a Steinbeck Fellowship in Creative Writing, among other honors. Previously an award-winning columnist for the San Francisco Chronicle, she teaches at the Warren Wilson MFA Program and elsewhere. This fall, she will be an Ann Getty Endowed Visiting-Artist Scholar at the University of San Francisco. Her debut book of narrative nonfiction, Uprooted, is forthcoming. Pronouns: She/Her ABOUT OPEN THE FLOODGATES “A beautiful story with an urgent message: that we must learn to champion the rights of the natural world with at least the same zeal as we do human rights. Nina Schuyler writes with a lyric intensity that practically sings from the page. The metaphorical register in which she chose to tell this story invited me to join the chorus.” — Claire Oshetsky, author of award-winning novels Chouette and Poor Deer We are in the midst of a profound legal shift: from New Zealand to India to Ecuador, real-world laws have granted personhood to rivers. With a mix of magic and pathos, Open the Floodgates imagines this new reality with a new configuration of the human and other-than-human relationship. In an unnamed California town, the River is granted personhood and has the right--and urgent need--to argue in court for its existence. But powerful, well-funded enemies are determined to keep the River exactly as it is: gunk-filled, toxic, a convenient dumping ground for waste. The story moves like water, entering the minds of the town's people, pigeons, deer, dogs, cats, the trees, the River's home, and the River itself. When the River moves, the text winds its way along the page, mimicking water. When the River is ultimately jailed, the town faces a reckoning: what do we owe the River? And the River must answer in turn: what, if anything, does it owe humans? ABOUT THE AUTHOR NINA SCHUYLER is the author of four other fiction books and teaches creative writing at Stanford Continuing Studies and the independent bookstore, Book Passage. Nina Schuyler's newest short story collection, In this Ravishing World, won the PEN Oakland Josephine Miles Literary Award, the W.S. Porter Prize for Short Story Collections, and the Prism Prize for Climate Literature. It was also a finalist for the Northern California Book Award. She graduated from Stanford University with a B.A. in Economics and earned a law degree at UC Law San Francisco. She is also the author of How to Write Stunning Sentences and has an extensive following of her Substack newsletter of the same name.

title: Stories We Carry
location: Petaluma Historical Library and Museum
description:
Every object has a story. Meet the people behind them. 

Multiple Dates: September 12 & 19, 6-8 pm

Petaluma Historical Library & Museum

20 4th Street \(Corner of 4th & B Street\)

Free Admission, Light refreshments will be served.

RSVP is recommended.

Join us for two special evenings with the community storytellers featured in Belongings: What We Bring, What We Leave Behind. Through family heirlooms, treasured keepsakes, photographs, letters, and everyday belongings, participants will share the deeply personal stories that bring the exhibition to life. 

Hear firsthand reflections on migration, identity, resilience, family, and the meaning of home. These intimate conversations offer a rare opportunity to connect directly with the individuals whose voices and objects are featured throughout the exhibition, creating space for dialogue, empathy, and shared understanding. 

Following the storytelling program, continue the conversation while exploring the exhibition and enjoying light refreshments. 

Stories We Carry is presented as part of Belongings: What We Bring, What We Leave Behind, on view September 4–October 4, 2026, at the Petaluma Historical Library & Museum. The exhibition explores migration, memory, and belonging through the meaningful objects and personal stories that connect us across generations and cultures. 

Belongings: What We Bring, What We Leave Behind is made possible through the generous support of California Humanities through its Connecting California grant program. We are also deeply grateful to our community partners and sponsors, including the North Bay Asian American Pacific Islander Coalition, Sonoma County Japanese American Citizens League, Petaluma Arts Center, Life on Art, Zimbabwe Cultural Exchange Project of California, El Día de los Muertos Petaluma, Bolca Avia, Chelsea Antiques, Café Puente, Rustic Bakery, Quality Inn Petaluma, and all of the organizations, volunteers, artists, and community members whose collaboration has brought this exhibition to life.

Marion will guide you through the basics of composition, color theory, and image selection. This workshop is designed for people of all creative levels who wish to learn collage and mixed media skills, connect with the community, and engage in meaningful self-expression. Students will have access to a curated selection of collage materials, paints, and scissors, and are encouraged to bring magazines and personal images of choice. This is a space for connection and non-judgement, where your unique creative expression matters above all - inviting curiosity and play to reveal new pathways of seeing and creating. Students are encouraged to bring the following materials: Gloves Preferred Glue Preferred scissorsAbout the Teacher: Marion Ruta Segal is Certified in Creative Arts Therapies  (The New School, NYC) and practicing mixed media artist with nearly 20 years of teaching experience in New York City and the San Francisco Bay Area. Her work includes painting, collage, and mixed media, and she has exhibited publicly since 2013. Marion has taught at community organizations and at the college level, leading workshops that invite students into exploratory, meaning-focused making - grounding them in core methods and aesthetics including design, color theory, and composition. title: Tom Chown: 46 Years Behind the Lens
location: Robert F. Agrella Art Gallery - Santa Rosa Campus
description: Santa Rosa Junior College will celebrate the 46-year career of longtime staff photographer Tom Chown with a photography exhibition featuring images from his decades at the college, from the days of film and darkrooms to the digital era.  Chown began his career at SRJC at age 24, working in the campus photography lab. Over the next 46 years, he became a familiar presence throughout the college community, documenting the people, programs and milestones that shaped generations of students and employees.  The exhibition will trace Chown's evolution as a photographer, from working with film and developing photographs in the darkroom to embracing digital photography. It also offers a visual history of SRJC, preserving moments from nearly five decades of college life.  The exhibition is free and open to the public.Location: Robert F. Agrella Art Gallery, Doyle Library 1st floor - Santa Rosa CampusFor more information, visit SRJC's Robert F. Agrella Art Gallery website. description:
September is the 17th Annual Pomo Honoring Month. On Monday, Sept. 14, the 6th California Native Creations Art Show opens Person Senior Wing, Finley Community Center, 2060 W. College Ave., Santa Rosa, CA. The show is free and open to the public Monday – Friday, 8:30 a.m.-4:30 p.m., through November 19.

The established and up-and-coming native artists create with digital media, paint and traditional materials in their art, weaving, regalia, beadwork, jewelry, baskets and quilts. The artists include:

·         Meyo Marrufo, painter, guest curator for the de Young Museum and the Sonoma Valley Art Museum,

·         Buffie Campbell, Vice Chair, Sherwood Valley Rancheria, cultural teacher and master basket maker,

·         Henry Edward Frank, Yurok/Kashaya Pomo, who will show paintings and work with Legos titled Mind Prison,

·         Digital artist Nicolas \(Nico\) Vargas, Kashia Band of Pomo Indians, whose art was featured at the 55th Annual Stanford Powwow.

·         plus Gloria Carretero; Rose Hammock; Rudy Hammock; Jocelyn Garcia; Arella Ortega LaRose, Kashia Band of Pomo Indians; Angelica Smith, Manchester Point Arena and Yokayo Rancheria; Maria Pasalo; Michelle Napoli; Martina Morgan, Kashia Band of Pomo Indians; Hands Lopez; Shashoni Hanover-Redenbaugh; Katie Williams-Elliott, Juan Partida, and Mia Pasalo, Big Valley Pomo Tribe.

**Yoga Vinyasa Krama - Thursdays 9-10:30am**

Physical Health, Conditioning, Pranic Flow, Vital Energy, Mental Focus & Stillness - through intelligent architecture with the metaphysics of deep conscious breathing & slow motion, yogic breathwork, mantra/sound/vibration, mudra, subtle & contemplative practices.
Yoga Vinyasa Krama is a comprehensive hatha-raja yogic system for purification, developing concentration, neuromuscular fitness and conditioning, refining & mastering the breath, awakening subtle energy and stilling the mind. Based on deep breathing & the subtle movement of prana directed into the cartilage tissue, sinuous musculature, internal organs, nerve pathways and nadis. It has over 700 intelligently sequenced slow, conscious breath powered with precision movement variations with pause (vinyasas), exploring many aesthetic variations of each posture to correctly establish the main asanas while the mind merges with the breath.
Includes the energetics of drishti, pratikriyas, bandha, vaseth, mudra, mantra, surya & ding namaskar with breath & mantra, cleansing kriyas, Himalayan pranayama including including ujjayi variations, heating & cooling breaths, solar, lunar & soli-lunar nadi shuddhi practices, pranava & samantraka pranayama, pratyahara, subtle & contemplative practices in 12 kramas (sequences).
The whole process gradually transforms the body and mind, releasing old patterns of physical and mental tension and dysfunctional patterns of movement, providing tonic, energetic and psychophysiological effects.
This system is presented from the teachings **Srivatsa Ramaswami** learned through his over 33 years of one on one study with **Sri Krishnamacharya** and teachings from a similar **Himalayan method**.
This ongoing class will explore the entire system of 12 Kramas with each class focusing on a particular krama or vinyasas from different kramas & pranayama & dharana practices.

title: Henry Frank: J-80928: A Human Experience Exhibition
location: San Geronimo Valley Community Center
description:
The San Geronimo Valley Community Center is proud to present featured September artist **Henry Frank** in the Del Mue Galleries this September. There will be a reception for the artist as part of the International Day of Peace Festival Finale on **September 20 from 2 – 6 pm**.

**J-80928: A Human Experience Exhibition** explores Henry Frank’s transformative journey through nearly three decades of incarceration in the California Department of Corrections. Through deeply personal artwork, the exhibition reflects on trauma, friendship, identity, hope, and personal growth while inviting viewers to recognize the humanity and capacity for change in people who are incarcerated.

**ARTISTS STATEMENT** **J-80928: A Human Experience Exhibition** explores my personal journey serving a 29-year-to-life sentence in the California Department of Corrections as an Indigenous person, an artist, and a human being. I was incarcerated from February 15, 1994, to April 19, 2013, and during much of that time, I lived hour to hour. For the first 14 years, my mantras were: expect the worst and hope for the best, trust no one except myself, and fear is a state of mind. While many experiences were deeply traumatic, there were also moments of humanity, compassion, joy, and empathy that transformed how I saw myself and the world around me.

The last six years of my incarceration became the most transformative period of my life. I began to believe that I would not die in prison. I found hope, discovered the importance of serving others, began to see myself as a serious artist, and gained a deeper understanding of my place in the world. My mantras evolved into: expect the best and be prepared for anything less, trust everyone until they give me a reason not to, and happiness is a choice. During this time, I learned to love and respect myself, to be accountable, to live in the present, to be a true friend, and to serve others with intention and compassion.

This exhibition is an oeuvre dedicated to the experiences, emotional trauma, friendships, and reclamation of identity that shaped me throughout my incarceration. Through this body of work, I hope people can connect with parts of my journey and recognize that I am not so different from them. More importantly, I want to humanize those who are currently incarcerated and raise awareness that people are capable of change. They can become contributing members of their communities. They have families, hobbies, hopes, dreams, and the capacity for growth and transformation.

I have been working toward completing this body of work and plan to have the exhibition finished completely by the end of this year.

This exhibition is partially funded by an Artist Fellowship Grant from the Art for Justice Fund. I am grateful for their support and patience for this exhibition to evolve into its fullest potential.

Human Being

Henry Edward Frank

Yurok and Kashaya Pomo

title: Cuentos con Ritmo (Stories with Rhythm)
location: Children's Museum of Sonoma County
description:
Cuentos con Ritmo \(Stories with Rhythm\)



Cuentos con Ritmo | Cuentos \* Música \* Movimiento 

Presentado por Colors of Spanish 

Cuentos con Ritmo es una oportunidad única semanal para niños de 1 a 5 años y sus familias, el cual aporta alegría, comprensión y aprecio por la lengua española a toda la comunidad. Durante Cuentos con Ritmo, los pequeños visitantes y sus familias participan de forma lúdica en historias interactivas con música y movimiento fortaleciendo nuestra diversa comunidad y entusiasmo por la lengua meta. 

Cuentos con Ritmo es presentado por Guadalupe Tausch en colaboración con la organización que fundó, Colors of Spanish. Originaria del estado de Guanajuato en México, tiene una maestría en español con énfasis en la adquisición de una segunda lengua para la primera infancia y continúa sus estudios enfocada en la primera infancia especializándose en la adquisición de idiomas a través de la música/movimiento. Colors of Spanish ofrece talleres para profesores, bibliotecarios y cuidadores y organiza programas de cuentos en español con música y movimiento en escuelas, bibliotecas y museos locales. www.colorsofspanish.org 

Cuentos con Ritmo | Cuentos \* Música \* Movimiento 

Presented by Colors of Spanish 

Cuentos con Ritmo \(Stories with Rhythm\) is a weekly one-of-a-kind opportunity for children ages 1-5 and their families that brings joy, understanding and appreciation for the Spanish language to Spanish- and English-speaking speakers alike. During Cuentos con Ritmo, young visitors and their families playfully engage in interactive stories with music and movement that build community and an excitement for language! 

Cuentos con Ritmo is presented by Guadalupe Tausch in collaboration with the organization she founded, Colors of Spanish. Originally from the state of Guanajuato in México, she has a master’s degree in Spanish with emphasis in second language acquisition for early childhood and continues her study of childhood and music/movement trainings. Colors of Spanish provides workshops for teachers, librarians and caregivers and hosts Spanish story time with music & movement programs at local schools, libraries, and museums. www.colorsofspanish.org 

Designed for kids 1-5, families, and siblings. 

 

Generously sponsored by RCU and the SABA Foundation.

title: A Taste of Italy at Centennial Mountain Tasting Room

description:
For wine drinkers eager to experience world-class wines made in California from Italian varieties, the Centennial Mountain Tasting Room is a must during any trip to Sonoma County. Located just off the plaza in the charming town of Healdsburg near famed restaurants, boutiques and galleries, the Centennial Mountain Tasting Room is a destination that invites discovery. Founded by the acclaimed team that guides renowned Pinot Noir and Chardonnay producer Rhys Vineyards, Centennial Mountain was established to explore Italian grape varieties grown on its acclaimed Centennial Mountain Vineyard in the rugged mountains of Northern Sonoma County.

The Centennial Mountain Vineyard Tasting features the winery’s coveted Nebbiolo, and the pioneering Carricante and Nerello Mascalese wines, among others. To showcase how beautifully the wines pair with food, the winery also offers a delicious Wine and Sushi Pairing from nearby Asahi Sushi, one of Healdsburg’s most popular dining destinations.

Guests can also enhance their tasting experience with a curated salumi board from Journeyman Meat Company. This generous accompaniment features six house-made salumi, crostini, cornichons, olives, and a selection of local cheese that serves 2 to 5 guests.

title: ART EXHIBIT:  THE DAYS OF VINES AND ROSES
location: Upstairs Art Gallery
description:
EPTEMBER ART EXHIBIT:  THE DAYS OF VINES AND ROSES

Date: FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE  8/12/26

DATES: August 31 – September 27, 2026

RECEPTION:  SATURDAY, September 5 – 3 -6 pm Join Donna Schaffer and Tosya Shore to celebrate the show and learn about their artistic inspirations.  Refreshments will be served.  

Featured Artist Donna Schaffer Celebrates Wine Country Beauty in “The Days of Vines and Roses”

Sonoma County artist Donna Schaffer unveils her latest collection of oil paintings, “The Days of Vines and Roses,” celebrating some of her favorite views of roses blooming among the vineyards, hills, and woodlands of Sonoma County. At the heart of the collection is Vines and Trellis of Roses, where glorious pink roses spill across an entrance trellis, set against the orderly rows of a vineyard. In Mini Red Roses Along Vineyard, delicate red roses punctuate the landscape, creating a lively interplay between vineyard rows, stands of trees, and the hills beyond. “Living here in Sonoma County for three decades, I never tire of its glorious natural beauty. It is an enduring inspiration and truly a painter’s dream,” says Schaffer.

Art has been a focus throughout Schaffer’s life. She has been painting full time in Dry Creek since the mid-1990s and is particularly known for her paintings of Sonoma County’s wine country. Her work are popular with both locals and visitors who want to bring a bit of Sonoma’s beauty and magic into their own homes. Schaffer has been a member of the Upstairs Art Gallery for more than 25 years and has exhibited regionally, including eight years as an Art Trails artist.

Meet the artist:  Schaffer will be hosting the Gallery on September 3 and 27 from 11-6 pm.  

Stairway Showcase: Tosya Shore — “It’s Black and White with a Splash of Color”

The Stairway Showcase presents artist Tosya Shore’s “It’s Black and White with a Splash of Color,” a collection of watercolors that begins with the fundamentals of composition: reducing an image to its two most essential elements—black and white. Working with ink, a stick, and a scraper, Shore roughens the edges of her subjects and strips away unnecessary detail, allowing light itself—not form or precision—to take center stage. Her paintings invite the viewer to experience the essence of a scene through contrast, gesture, and the expressive qualities of the medium.

In addition to her watercolor works, Shore presents paintings inspired by a recent trip to Carmel, where she picked up oil paint for the first time and explored painting the ocean using nothing but a palette knife. The resulting works introduce a vibrant splash of color and texture into a practice grounded in restraint—new pigment, new surface, yet the same enduring fascination with light over likeness.

description:

Unlock your inner strength and find your flow. Belly dancing with Raja is an innovative fusion class that blends the rhythmic artistry of belly dance with the high-energy benefits of aerobics. Designed to be both a cardiovascular challenge and a deep toning session, this class focuses on the “powerhouse” of the body—your core.

By layering fluid, isolative movements over an athletic aerobic base, you will challenge your muscles in ways traditional gym workouts can’t reach.

What to Expect in Belly Dancing Class

• Core-Centric Power: Use undulations and shimmies to engage deep abdominal muscles for a tighter, stronger midsection.

• Functional Stability: Improve your balance and posture through controlled, hip-driven movements and low-impact aerobic footwork.

• Total Body Toning: Build lean muscle in your legs, glutes, and arms while maintaining a constant, heart-pumping pace.

• Mind-Body Connection: Enhance your coordination and body awareness through rhythmic, expressive choreography.

“Whether you’re looking to define your waistline or simply want a workout that feels like a celebration, this class offers the perfect balance of sweat and grace.”

Difficulty Level: All levels welcome! No prior dance experience is required—just bring your energy and a willingness to move.

title: Napa Bookmine Book Club: Angel Down by Daniel Kraus
location: Napa Bookmine
description: Join us for a book club discussion! This year, 2026, Napa Bookmine Book Clubs' book picks will come straight from home, this year's Napa Bookmine BINGO Card! Each book will match a BINGO square. Hurrah! Play along with Napa Bookmine and read some new, fun books, and if you come to every meeting, you may get a BINGO in the meantime. ;\) This is a free event, but we would appreciate your RSVP so we can plan for your attendance! Questions? Email us at events@napabookmine.com ABOUT THE BOOK WINNER OF THE PULITZER PRIZE FOR FICTION NEW YORK TIMES TOP TEN BOOKS OF 2025 NATIONAL BESTSELLER The critically acclaimed author of the “crazily enjoyable” \(The New York Times\) Whalefall returns with an immersive, cinematic novel about five World War I soldiers who stumble upon a fallen angel that could hold the key to ending the war. Private Cyril Bagger has managed to survive the unspeakable horrors of the Great War through his wits and deception. But his survival instincts are put to the ultimate test when he and four other grunts are given a deadly mission: venture into the perilous No Man’s Land to euthanize a wounded comrade. What they find amid the ruined battlefield, however, is not a man in need of mercy but a fallen angel, seemingly struck down by artillery fire. This celestial being may hold the key to ending the brutal conflict, but only if the soldiers can suppress their individual desires and work together. As jealousy, greed, and paranoia take hold, the group is torn apart by their inner demons, threatening to turn their angelic encounter into a descent into hell. Angel Down plunges you into the heart of World War I and weaves a polyphonic tale of survival, supernatural wonder, and moral conflict. ABOUT THE AUTHOR Daniel Kraus is a New York Times bestselling writer of novels, TV, and film. His novel Whalefall received a front-cover review in The New York Times Book Review, won the Alex Award, was an LA Times Book Prize Finalist, and was a Best Book of 2023 from NPR, The New York Times, Chicago Tribune, and more. With Guillermo del Toro, he coauthored The Shape of Water, based on the same idea the two created for the Oscar–winning film. Also with del Toro, Kraus coauthored Trollhunters, which was adapted into the Emmy-winning Netflix series. He also cowrote The Living Dead and Pay the Piper with legendary filmmaker George A. Romero. Kraus’s The Death and Life of Zebulon Finch was named one of Entertainment Weekly’s Top 10 Books of the Year. Kraus has won the Bram Stoker Award, Scribe Award, two Odyssey Awards \(for both Rotters and Scowler\), and has appeared multiple times as Library Guild selections, YALSA Best Fiction for Young Adults, and more. His work has been translated into over twenty languages. He lives with his wife in Chicago. Visit him at DanielKraus.com.

title: Stories We Carry
location: Petaluma Historical Library and Museum
description:
Every object has a story. Meet the people behind them. 

Multiple Dates: September 12 & 19, 6-8 pm

Petaluma Historical Library & Museum

20 4th Street \(Corner of 4th & B Street\)

Free Admission, Light refreshments will be served.

RSVP is recommended.

Join us for two special evenings with the community storytellers featured in Belongings: What We Bring, What We Leave Behind. Through family heirlooms, treasured keepsakes, photographs, letters, and everyday belongings, participants will share the deeply personal stories that bring the exhibition to life. 

Hear firsthand reflections on migration, identity, resilience, family, and the meaning of home. These intimate conversations offer a rare opportunity to connect directly with the individuals whose voices and objects are featured throughout the exhibition, creating space for dialogue, empathy, and shared understanding. 

Following the storytelling program, continue the conversation while exploring the exhibition and enjoying light refreshments. 

Stories We Carry is presented as part of Belongings: What We Bring, What We Leave Behind, on view September 4–October 4, 2026, at the Petaluma Historical Library & Museum. The exhibition explores migration, memory, and belonging through the meaningful objects and personal stories that connect us across generations and cultures. 

Belongings: What We Bring, What We Leave Behind is made possible through the generous support of California Humanities through its Connecting California grant program. We are also deeply grateful to our community partners and sponsors, including the North Bay Asian American Pacific Islander Coalition, Sonoma County Japanese American Citizens League, Petaluma Arts Center, Life on Art, Zimbabwe Cultural Exchange Project of California, El Día de los Muertos Petaluma, Bolca Avia, Chelsea Antiques, Café Puente, Rustic Bakery, Quality Inn Petaluma, and all of the organizations, volunteers, artists, and community members whose collaboration has brought this exhibition to life.

You will learn

The Basic Step: You will master the signature quick-quick-slow rhythm that defines Samba no Pé.

Arm & Hip Styling: You will learn how to add the authentic flair, movement, and energy that makes Brazilian samba so captivating.

This class is perfect for anyone looking to connect with the vibrant spirit of Brazil, improve coordination, and get a fantastic workout—all while learning the foundational steps of this iconic dance. description:
We meet in-person only on the 1st and 2nd Thursdays of the month. However, you can catch us online every Thursday unless the meeting date falls on a holiday.

Please register at https://signup.com/go/WiniixA

What is Toastmasters About?

Usually at our meetings, we will have a prepared speech, and a speech evaluation. The Grammarian and Wizard of Ah's will listen for turns of phrases and the use of filler words. We also practice impromptu speaking during the section of the meeting called Table Topics. During Table Topics, at a recent meeting, we were asked what we felt was the biggest communication problem or challenge. What would you answer in a fast moment? Table topics will challenge you to think quickly and give an answer without preparation.

You will also hear tips on public speaking skills at our upcoming meeting. Whether you're a seasoned traveler or just looking for some adventure from the comfort of your home, this event is perfect for you.

Toastmasters International is all about communication excellence, and for 100 years and counting, Toastmasters have been expressing themselves better, practicing, and evaluating in a fun club environment, shining all around the world.

title: South Pacific
location: 6th Street Playhouse
description:
**An unforgettable romance set against the sweeping tides of World War II.**

Against the backdrop of the Pacific War of WWII, ***South Pacific*** blends high-stakes wartime romance with a poignant exploration of social prejudice. When spirited Navy nurse, Nellie Forbush, falls in love with a sophisticated French planter, and a young Marine lieutenant finds himself captivated by an ethereal island girl, their relationships are tested by the prejudices and pressures of a world at war. What unfolds is a deeply moving story about love, courage, and the transformative power of understanding. Featuring a soaring score by **Richard Rodgers** and **Oscar Hammerstein II**, including classics like “Some Enchanted Evening” and “There Is Nothin’ Like a Dame,” *South Pacific* remains one of the most beloved musicals of all time.

Winner of the 1950 Pulitzer Prize for Drama, the original Broadway production won ten Tony Awards, including Best Musical, Best Score and Best Libretto. It is the only musical production ever to have won all four Tony Awards for acting.

SOUTH PACIFIC is presented by arrangement with Concord Theatricals on behalf of The Rodgers & Hammerstein Organization. concordtheatricals.com

Performances run Thur, Friday, Saturday evenings at 7:30pm and Saturday and Sunday matinees at 2:00pm.

title: Vieux Farka Touré
location: Mystic Theatre & Music Hall
description:
**Vieux Farka Touré** 

Often referred to as “The Hendrix of the Sahara”, Vieux Farka Touré was born in Niafunké, Mali in 1981. He is the son of legendary Malian guitar player Ali Farka Touré, who died in 2006. Ali Farka Touré came from a historical tribe of soldiers, and defied his parents in becoming a musician. When Vieux was in his teens, he declared that he also wanted to be a musician. His father disapproved due to the pressures he had experienced being a musician. Rather, he wanted Vieux to become a soldier. But with help from family friend the kora maestro Toumani Diabaté, Vieux eventually convinced his father to give him his blessing to become a musician shortly before Ali passed.

Vieux was initially a drummer / calabash player at Mali’s Institut National des Arts, but secretly began playing guitar in 2001. Ali Farka Touré was weakened with cancer when Vieux announced that he was going to record an album. Ali recorded a couple of tracks with him, and these recordings, which can be heard on Vieux’s debut CD, were amongst his final ones. It has been said that the senior Touré played rough mixes of these songs when people visited him in his final days, at peace with, and proud of, his son’s talent as a musician.

In 2005, Eric Herman (still Vieux’s manager today) of Modiba Productions expressed an interest in producing an album for Vieux; this led to Vieux’s self-titled debut album, released by World Village in 2007. Ali Farka Touré’s work to tackle the problem of malaria is continued as 10% of proceeds are donated to Modiba’s “Fight Malaria” campaign in Niafunké through which over 3000 mosquito nets have been delivered to children and pregnant women in the Timbuktu region of Mali. On this first album, Vieux pays homage to his father and follows Ali’s musical tradition, giving new versions of the West African music that is echoed in the American blues. The album features Toumani Diabaté, as well as his late father.

On his second record, Fondo on Six Degrees (2009), Vieux branched out and presented his own sound: while remaining true to the roots of his father’s music he uses elements of rock, Latin music, and other African influences. The album received a great deal of critical acclaim from across the globe, and Vieux was clearly moving out of his father’s shadow.

By June 2010, Vieux was performing at the opening concert for the FIFA World Cup in South Africa. That month Vieux also released his first live album, LIVE. His live performances are highly energized and Vieux is known for dazzling crowds with his speed and dexterity on the guitar, as well as his palpable charisma and luminous smile, both of which captivate audiences from all audiences in spite of any language barriers (though Vieux does speak 8 languages).

In 2011 Vieux released his 3rd studio album, The Secret, so named because the listener will hear the secret of the blues with a blend of generations from father to son. It was produced by guitarist Eric Krasno (of the Soulive trio) and features South African-born vocalist Dave Matthews, Derek Trucks on electric slide guitar and jazz guitarist John Scofield. The title track is the last collaboration between Vieux and his late father. With the heralded release of The Secret, Vieux Farka Touré has clearly established himself as one of the world’s rare musical talents and guitar virtuosos with a distinct style that always pays homage to the past while looking towards the future.

Vieux released The Tel Aviv Session (Cumbancha) in April 2012, a collaborative project with Israeli superstar Idan Raichel dubbed ‘The Touré-Raichel Collective’ that has been hailed by fans and critics alike as a masterpiece and one of the best collaborative albums in the history of international music, drawing comparisons to Ali Farka Touré and Ry Cooder’s legendary Talking Timbuktu album.

In 2013, Vieux Farka Touré’s beautiful and critically acclaimed album Mon Pays was released as an homage to his homeland. Being that his native Mali had recently been splintered by territorial fighting between Tuareg and Islamic rebels since January 2012, Mon Pays was devoted to reminding the world about the beauty and culture of his native Mali. Translated as ‘My Country,’ this predominantly acoustic undertaking transformed into an artifact of cultural preservation. Two songs on the project - ‘Future’ and ‘Peace’ feature Sidiki Diabate’s kora leading an emotional charge complemented by Touré’s spectacular guitar work. Both tracks represent an important generational “passing of the torch” as Sidiki’s father, Toumani is considered one of the greatest living kora masters and was a close friend of Vieux’s father Ali. Mon Pays has been widely hailed as the most mature and lovely record yet from one of this generation’s most exciting artists to come out of Mali and one of world music’s true rising stars.

Vieux reunited with Idan Raichel in Paris to record, release and subsequently tour their 2nd collaborative album as The Touré-Raichel Collective in 2014. The result was yet another musical and critical triumph, titled 'The Paris Session' (Cumbancha) revered by many as not just a musical gem for the ages, but a powerful testimonial to the power of art and fraternity to transcend vast cultural and political divides. In 2015, Vieux released another unexpected, genre-bending collaborative album, this time with New York-based singer Julia Easterlin, aptly titled 'Touristes'. The album shot to the top of the iTunes World chart and earned critical acclaim, including that of John Schaefer (NPR) who called it "brilliant." On April 7, 2017, Vieux released his next album 'Samba', recorded live in front of a small audience at Applehead Studio in Woodstock, NY.

When the COVID pandemic hit in 2020 and all touring ground to a halt, Vieux stayed focussed on his craft at home. He worked tirelessly in the studio he built at his family's compound (which he named 'Studio Ali Farka Toure' in honor of his late father) to record his debut album for World Circuit Records/BMG, the prestigious UK-based record label with whom his father recorded and released most of his own work. The resulting album, 'Les Racines' (released June 2022), sees Vieux masterfully return to the deep roots of the Desert Blues music that his father introduced to the world and Vieux spent most of his career to date exploring, experimenting with, and expanding. 2022 also saw the release of a long-awaited collaborative album between Vieux and Houston-based psych-rock superstars Khruangbin called ‘Ali’ - an album on which the artists join forces to pay homage to Ali Farka Toure by reimagining eight of his songs together. The album was an instant hit around the globe, immediately getting millions of streams, enormous critical acclaim and even earning the praise of Sir Elton John who called it "one of the albums of the year - absolutely wonderful music." With each new project Vieux broadens his horizons, embraces new challenges and further entrenches his reputation as one of the world’s most talented and innovative musicians.

As a passionate champion for the people of Mali and The Sahel, Vieux founded the charity Amahrec Sahel in 2012. As part of Amahrec Sahel’s mission to support humanitarian reconstruction and culture, the charity has provided school supplies for children, supported an orphanage in Bamako and provided musical instruments for young musicians in Mali. Vieux is also the director of The Ali Farka Touré Foundation, an international organization dedicated to the preservation of Ali’s legacy and the cultural growth of Mali.

title: California Native Creations Art Show

description:
September is the 17th Annual Pomo Honoring Month. On Monday, Sept. 14, the 6th California Native Creations Art Show opens Person Senior Wing, Finley Community Center, 2060 W. College Ave., Santa Rosa, CA. The show is free and open to the public Monday – Friday, 8:30 a.m.-4:30 p.m., through November 19.

The established and up-and-coming native artists create with digital media, paint and traditional materials in their art, weaving, regalia, beadwork, jewelry, baskets and quilts. The artists include:

·         Meyo Marrufo, painter, guest curator for the de Young Museum and the Sonoma Valley Art Museum,

·         Buffie Campbell, Vice Chair, Sherwood Valley Rancheria, cultural teacher and master basket maker,

·         Henry Edward Frank, Yurok/Kashaya Pomo, who will show paintings and work with Legos titled Mind Prison,

·         Digital artist Nicolas \(Nico\) Vargas, Kashia Band of Pomo Indians, whose art was featured at the 55th Annual Stanford Powwow.

·         plus Gloria Carretero; Rose Hammock; Rudy Hammock; Jocelyn Garcia; Arella Ortega LaRose, Kashia Band of Pomo Indians; Angelica Smith, Manchester Point Arena and Yokayo Rancheria; Maria Pasalo; Michelle Napoli; Martina Morgan, Kashia Band of Pomo Indians; Hands Lopez; Shashoni Hanover-Redenbaugh; Katie Williams-Elliott, Juan Partida, and Mia Pasalo, Big Valley Pomo Tribe.

title: Formative Influence Art Exhibit
location: Marin Center
description: Formative Influence explores the transformative power of light across five bodies of work. Inspired by the landscapes of Northern California and the American West, the exhibition examines the shift from photography, where light is observed and captured, to painting, where light is created to shape new visual experiences. Rather than documenting the landscape, these works evoke its emotional resonance, emphasizing atmosphere, memory, and perception over literal representation.

title: Henry Frank: J-80928: A Human Experience Exhibition
location: San Geronimo Valley Community Center
description:
The San Geronimo Valley Community Center is proud to present featured September artist **Henry Frank** in the Del Mue Galleries this September. There will be a reception for the artist as part of the International Day of Peace Festival Finale on **September 20 from 2 – 6 pm**.

**J-80928: A Human Experience Exhibition** explores Henry Frank’s transformative journey through nearly three decades of incarceration in the California Department of Corrections. Through deeply personal artwork, the exhibition reflects on trauma, friendship, identity, hope, and personal growth while inviting viewers to recognize the humanity and capacity for change in people who are incarcerated.

**ARTISTS STATEMENT** **J-80928: A Human Experience Exhibition** explores my personal journey serving a 29-year-to-life sentence in the California Department of Corrections as an Indigenous person, an artist, and a human being. I was incarcerated from February 15, 1994, to April 19, 2013, and during much of that time, I lived hour to hour. For the first 14 years, my mantras were: expect the worst and hope for the best, trust no one except myself, and fear is a state of mind. While many experiences were deeply traumatic, there were also moments of humanity, compassion, joy, and empathy that transformed how I saw myself and the world around me.

The last six years of my incarceration became the most transformative period of my life. I began to believe that I would not die in prison. I found hope, discovered the importance of serving others, began to see myself as a serious artist, and gained a deeper understanding of my place in the world. My mantras evolved into: expect the best and be prepared for anything less, trust everyone until they give me a reason not to, and happiness is a choice. During this time, I learned to love and respect myself, to be accountable, to live in the present, to be a true friend, and to serve others with intention and compassion.

This exhibition is an oeuvre dedicated to the experiences, emotional trauma, friendships, and reclamation of identity that shaped me throughout my incarceration. Through this body of work, I hope people can connect with parts of my journey and recognize that I am not so different from them. More importantly, I want to humanize those who are currently incarcerated and raise awareness that people are capable of change. They can become contributing members of their communities. They have families, hobbies, hopes, dreams, and the capacity for growth and transformation.

I have been working toward completing this body of work and plan to have the exhibition finished completely by the end of this year.

This exhibition is partially funded by an Artist Fellowship Grant from the Art for Justice Fund. I am grateful for their support and patience for this exhibition to evolve into its fullest potential.

Human Being

Henry Edward Frank

Yurok and Kashaya Pomo

title: A Taste of Italy at Centennial Mountain Tasting Room
location: Centennial Mountain Tasting Room
description:
For wine drinkers eager to experience world-class wines made in California from Italian varieties, the Centennial Mountain Tasting Room is a must during any trip to Sonoma County. Located just off the plaza in the charming town of Healdsburg near famed restaurants, boutiques and galleries, the Centennial Mountain Tasting Room is a destination that invites discovery. Founded by the acclaimed team that guides renowned Pinot Noir and Chardonnay producer Rhys Vineyards, Centennial Mountain was established to explore Italian grape varieties grown on its acclaimed Centennial Mountain Vineyard in the rugged mountains of Northern Sonoma County.

The Centennial Mountain Vineyard Tasting features the winery’s coveted Nebbiolo, and the pioneering Carricante and Nerello Mascalese wines, among others. To showcase how beautifully the wines pair with food, the winery also offers a delicious Wine and Sushi Pairing from nearby Asahi Sushi, one of Healdsburg’s most popular dining destinations.

Guests can also enhance their tasting experience with a curated salumi board from Journeyman Meat Company. This generous accompaniment features six house-made salumi, crostini, cornichons, olives, and a selection of local cheese that serves 2 to 5 guests.

title: ART EXHIBIT:  THE DAYS OF VINES AND ROSES
location: Upstairs Art Gallery
description:
EPTEMBER ART EXHIBIT:  THE DAYS OF VINES AND ROSES

Date: FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE  8/12/26

DATES: August 31 – September 27, 2026

RECEPTION:  SATURDAY, September 5 – 3 -6 pm Join Donna Schaffer and Tosya Shore to celebrate the show and learn about their artistic inspirations.  Refreshments will be served.  

Featured Artist Donna Schaffer Celebrates Wine Country Beauty in “The Days of Vines and Roses”

Sonoma County artist Donna Schaffer unveils her latest collection of oil paintings, “The Days of Vines and Roses,” celebrating some of her favorite views of roses blooming among the vineyards, hills, and woodlands of Sonoma County. At the heart of the collection is Vines and Trellis of Roses, where glorious pink roses spill across an entrance trellis, set against the orderly rows of a vineyard. In Mini Red Roses Along Vineyard, delicate red roses punctuate the landscape, creating a lively interplay between vineyard rows, stands of trees, and the hills beyond. “Living here in Sonoma County for three decades, I never tire of its glorious natural beauty. It is an enduring inspiration and truly a painter’s dream,” says Schaffer.

Art has been a focus throughout Schaffer’s life. She has been painting full time in Dry Creek since the mid-1990s and is particularly known for her paintings of Sonoma County’s wine country. Her work are popular with both locals and visitors who want to bring a bit of Sonoma’s beauty and magic into their own homes. Schaffer has been a member of the Upstairs Art Gallery for more than 25 years and has exhibited regionally, including eight years as an Art Trails artist.

Meet the artist:  Schaffer will be hosting the Gallery on September 3 and 27 from 11-6 pm.  

Stairway Showcase: Tosya Shore — “It’s Black and White with a Splash of Color”

The Stairway Showcase presents artist Tosya Shore’s “It’s Black and White with a Splash of Color,” a collection of watercolors that begins with the fundamentals of composition: reducing an image to its two most essential elements—black and white. Working with ink, a stick, and a scraper, Shore roughens the edges of her subjects and strips away unnecessary detail, allowing light itself—not form or precision—to take center stage. Her paintings invite the viewer to experience the essence of a scene through contrast, gesture, and the expressive qualities of the medium.

In addition to her watercolor works, Shore presents paintings inspired by a recent trip to Carmel, where she picked up oil paint for the first time and explored painting the ocean using nothing but a palette knife. The resulting works introduce a vibrant splash of color and texture into a practice grounded in restraint—new pigment, new surface, yet the same enduring fascination with light over likeness.

Join us virtually for an hour + of writing using Zoom. Let's keep together as much as we can during these uncertain times and keep on writing. Look for the schedule online and join us.

around 3:10 - timer starts: write for 70 mins.

description:
This fall, Buena Vista Winery invites you to uncover the mysteries, legends, and ghostly encounters woven into more than 165 years of history. Led by Sonoma historian and actor George Webber, this immersive 90 minute experience journeys through the historic Press House and Champagne Cellars, revealing true tales of unexplained happenings reported by Buena Vista team members and visitors throughout the years.

Hear the stories of the Glowing Ghostly Shirt, the Little Girl Who Says Hi, the mysterious Ghost Party on the Second Floor, the Old Man Who Walked Into a Stone Wall, and other strange occurrences that continue to add to the legend of Buena Vista.

Along the way, explore some of the winery’s most intriguing spaces, including the Bubble Lounge, Cave of Curiosities, and Wine Tool Museum, while enjoying five Buena Vista wines tasted throughout the experience, including a taste drawn directly from barrel.

And, as with any journey through Buena Vista’s extraordinary past, you never quite know when the winery’s legendary founder, Count Agoston Haraszthy, may choose to make an appearance.

History, wine, mystery, and perhaps a spirit or two await.

title: When I Am Among the Trees - Opening Reception
location: Western Hills Garden
description:
Join us for the opening reception of When I Am Among the Trees, a site-specific installation by artist Natalie Joy Tremblay.

Created using cyanotype textiles made with plant materials gathered from Western Hills Garden, the installation unfolds throughout the landscape as a series of large-format works that invite visitors to slow down, notice light and movement, and experience the garden in a new way.

Emerging as an extension of the living collection, each piece encourages reflection on the beauty of moments that cannot be held, only experienced.

Celebrate the opening with the artist, enjoy wine and light refreshments, and be among the first to experience this temporary exhibition at golden hour.

Visitors will receive a commemorative exhibition postcard and map to guide their exploration of the installation. All works will be for sale at the end of the three-day installation.

The reception is free and open to the public; registration is required.

Artist Bio: Natalie Joy Tremblay is a Sonoma County–based cyanotype artist whose work explores the relationship between plants, light, and place. Working with fresh flowers, foliage, and sunlight, she creates one-of-a-kind botanical artworks that celebrate seasonality, impermanence, and the quiet wonder of the natural world.

Inspired by the rhythms of the landscape, Natalie's practice embraces the unexpected, allowing light and chemistry to capture moments that can never be repeated. Her work invites viewers to slow down, reconnect with nature, and discover beauty in what is here, now, and ever-changing. She teaches cyanotype workshops throughout Sonoma County, including at Western Hills Garden, and her work has been exhibited in local galleries and collected by nature lovers across the country..

title: SQFF & International Day of Peace Festival present : Healing Through Hula
location: San Geronimo Valley Community Center
description:
The San Geronimo Valley Community Center's International Day of Peace Festival weekend begins with a special screening of the documentary feature Healing Through Hula, presented by the San Quentin Film Festival. The film sets the tone for a weekend dedicated to exploring the many pathways to peace.

Directed by Louis Sále, Healing Through Hula tells the powerful story of Asian American and Pacific Islander men in prison who reconnect with their cultural heritage through the practice of hula. Drawing from his own lived experience, Sále chronicles a journey of healing and redemption that culminates in a moving Makahiki ceremonial ritual. The original 10-minute version of the film was first screened at the inaugural San Quentin Film Festival \(SQFF\) in 2024, where it received the award for Best Documentary Short. The evening program will include two additional short films: Processing, a SQFF25 Short Film Finalist, directed by formerly incarcerated filmmaker, artist and musician Antwan Banks Williamsand Exonerated, directed by incarcerated filmmaker Ernest “Ben Shua”Woods II. 

Following the film, attendees are invited to stay for a panel discussion featuring director Antwan Williams and Demora Henderson, the subject of Exonerated, who was released in June and continues the struggle to overturn his wrongful conviction. The conversation will be moderated by the Community Center's own Alexa Davidson.

Prior to the screening, at 5:30pm guests are invited to enjoy a reception where the Lagunitas Middle School eighth-grade class will offer refreshments as a fundraiser for their Spring 2027 Civil Rights Field Trip.

Healing Through Hula begins at 6:30pm sharp!

title: SUP Yoga on the Petaluma River
location: The Floathouse Petaluma
description:
Slow down and float into a quieter rhythm with SUP Yoga on the Petaluma River at The Floathouse Petaluma. Launching from downtown Petaluma, this peaceful on-the-water yoga experience feels worlds away from the bustle—set in the calm, protected turning basin where the river naturally invites you to relax.

This all-levels, 90-minute session welcomes everyone, from first-time paddle boarders and yoga newcomers to experienced practitioners. We begin with a short, gentle paddle from the docks to get comfortable on your board \(knees are always welcome\), then anchor together so tidal movement won’t interrupt your flow. Once settled, you’re free to move, stretch, rest, or simply be—guided by expert instruction and supported by the shared energy of the group. Evening sessions and morning sessions allow YOU to choose the vibe that suits you best.

All equipment is provided, including extra-stable paddleboards that are wider and longer than a yoga mat, designed to help you feel grounded and secure on the water.

Perfect for locals and Bay Area visitors alike, SUP Yoga on the Petaluma River offers a rare chance to experience downtown Petaluma from the water—peaceful, playful, and deeply restorative.

It’s YOUR river. Come out and play.

title: Stories We Carry
location: Petaluma Historical Library and Museum
description:
Every object has a story. Meet the people behind them. 

Multiple Dates: September 12 & 19, 6-8 pm

Petaluma Historical Library & Museum

20 4th Street \(Corner of 4th & B Street\)

Free Admission, Light refreshments will be served.

RSVP is recommended.

Join us for two special evenings with the community storytellers featured in Belongings: What We Bring, What We Leave Behind. Through family heirlooms, treasured keepsakes, photographs, letters, and everyday belongings, participants will share the deeply personal stories that bring the exhibition to life. 

Hear firsthand reflections on migration, identity, resilience, family, and the meaning of home. These intimate conversations offer a rare opportunity to connect directly with the individuals whose voices and objects are featured throughout the exhibition, creating space for dialogue, empathy, and shared understanding. 

Following the storytelling program, continue the conversation while exploring the exhibition and enjoying light refreshments. 

Stories We Carry is presented as part of Belongings: What We Bring, What We Leave Behind, on view September 4–October 4, 2026, at the Petaluma Historical Library & Museum. The exhibition explores migration, memory, and belonging through the meaningful objects and personal stories that connect us across generations and cultures. 

Belongings: What We Bring, What We Leave Behind is made possible through the generous support of California Humanities through its Connecting California grant program. We are also deeply grateful to our community partners and sponsors, including the North Bay Asian American Pacific Islander Coalition, Sonoma County Japanese American Citizens League, Petaluma Arts Center, Life on Art, Zimbabwe Cultural Exchange Project of California, El Día de los Muertos Petaluma, Bolca Avia, Chelsea Antiques, Café Puente, Rustic Bakery, Quality Inn Petaluma, and all of the organizations, volunteers, artists, and community members whose collaboration has brought this exhibition to life.

description:
HEMMED UP is a punk rock band hailing from the mean streets of the Bay Area in Northern California,. It takes a lot to cut through the white noise in an area that is so culturally and musically prolific, and hemmed up achieves just that with songs about life on a road less traveled, dealing with self inflicted wounds, and commiserating about good times and bad. All of this, backed by a charged blend of outlaw music, ska, and punk, sets the stage for rowdy crowd participation and a truly memorable show! Only bonafide punks should be able to play punk rock, and only bonafide outlaws should be able to play outlaw music, and HEMMED UP checks all the boxes! Whiskey fueled and gritty lyrics backed by insane bass lines, shit hot guitar licks, and drum beats that would make Animal from the muppet’s head spin! This all lends perfectly to the anthemic, anti-authoritarian, Robin Hood mentality that their music has to offer…. There are 1312 reasons to love Hemmed Up! New full length album is available digitally 6/25/24.

Hemmed up has played many headline shows, and has shared the stage with an ever growing list of touring and regional bands like Get Dead, Jen Pop \(from the bombpops\), Hunting Lions, Surprise Privilege, Öil!, Fox Medicine, The Quitters, and many more!

title: Henry Kramer - Solo Piano
description: Henry Kramer, pianist, has been praised by The Cleveland Classical Review for his "astonishingly confident technique" and by The New York Times for "thrilling and triumphant" performances. Known for his sensitivity, stylish programming, and insightful interpretations, he gained international recognition with Second Prize at the 2016 Queen Elisabeth Competition and received a 2019 Avery Fisher Career Grant. A native of Cape Elizabeth, Maine, Kramer began piano at age 11, quickly advancing from self-taught beginnings to studying Chopin and Mozart. He went on to win major competitions including the National Chopin \(2010\), Montreal International \(2011\), and Shanghai International \(2012\), later earning top honors at the Honens Competition and joining Astral Artists. Kramer has performed widely as a soloist and recitalist, with notable debuts at Alice Tully Hall and Amsterdam's Concertgebouw. He has appeared with orchestras such as the Belgian National, Shanghai Philharmonic, and Indianapolis Symphony, collaborating with leading conductors including Marin Alsop and Stéphane Denève. His active recital schedule includes major venues and festivals across North America and beyond, with highlights in the 2025-26 season including performances with the Baton Rouge Symphony, Chamber Orchestra of Philadelphia, and appearances in New York, Montreal, Seattle, and Washington, D.C. An accomplished chamber musician, Kramer has performed with the Chamber Music Society of Lincoln Center and collaborated with artists including Emmanuel Pahud and the Calidore Quartet. His recordings have received critical acclaim from BBC Music Magazine and Gramophone. Kramer is also a dedicated educator, joining the Université de Montréal faculty in 2022 after previous positions at Columbus State University, Smith College, and the University of Missouri-Kansas City. He holds degrees from Juilliard and Yale, where he studied with Julian Martin, Robert McDonald, and Boris Berman. A Steinway Artist, his pedagogical lineage traces back to Beethoven, Chopin, and Busoni.
